original_authors: Feldman-Summers, S.; Pope, K.
original_title: The experience of 'forgetting' child abuse: A national survey of psychologists
original_journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
description: Among psychologists who reported experiencing childhood abuse, approximately 40% experienced a period of forgetting some or all of the abuse for a significant period of time
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion section: 'Virtually the same percentages of Dutch (39%) and US psychologists (41%; Feldman-Summers and Pope, 1994) reported some significant period of forgetting abuse.' The abstract concludes: 'These results were remarkably similar to the results of Feldman-Summers and Pope's original study.'

original_authors: Nahari, G.; Vrij, A.; Fisher, R.
original_title: The verifiability approach: Countermeasures facilitate its ability to discriminate between truths and lies
description: When forewarned that their statements would be checked for verifiable details, truth tellers provide more verifiable details than liars
justification: The authors explicitly state: "Following our predefined replication criterion, we consider the replication successful: Being forewarned, truth tellers provided significantly more verifiable details than liars" and "Four researchers (BV, MS, IK, SVO) were involved in this replication, and all four considered the replication successful."

original_authors: Murdock, N.; Edwards, C.; Murdock, T.
original_title: Therapists' attributions for client premature termination: Are they self-serving?
description: Therapists exhibit self-serving bias when evaluating premature treatment termination, attributing more blame to client characteristics when evaluating their own clients and more blame to therapist factors when evaluating other therapists' clients
justification: The authors explicitly state: 'In contrast to Murdock et al. (2010), we did not find evidence for a general SSB in therapists' attributions' and conclude 'The present study did not find evidence for a robust SSB in therapists' evaluation of causes for premature treatment termination.' The critical interaction effect that would indicate self-serving bias was non-significant (F(2, 88) = .75, p = .48).

original_authors: Sfärlea, A.; Greimel, E.; Platt, B.; Dieler, A.; Schulte-Körne, G.
original_title: Recognition of emotional facial expressions in adolescents with anorexia nervosa and adolescents with major depression
description: Adolescents with anorexia nervosa show superior facial emotion recognition abilities compared to adolescents without mental disorders, with higher accuracy specifically for afraid facial expressions
justification: The authors explicitly state: "We found the same pattern of results as in our previous study [31] in an independent sample of adolescents with and without AN, allowing us to interpret our results with more confidence" and "we succeeded in exactly replicating the pattern of results."

original_authors: Van Doornik, S.; Glashouwer, K.; Ostafin, B.; De Jong, P. J.
original_title: The Effects of a Meaning-Centered Intervention on Meaning in Life and Eating Disorder Symptoms in Undergraduate Women With High Weight and Shape Concerns: A Randomized Controlled Trial
description: A 6-week online meaning-centered intervention increases life meaning and reduces eating disorder symptoms and general distress in young women with weight and shape concerns
justification: The authors explicitly state: "our study demonstrated replicational evidence for the efficacy of a meaning-centered intervention in terms of higher life meaning for young women with weight and shape concerns." The primary outcome (life meaning) replicated successfully at both post-assessment (η²p = 0.23) and follow-up (η²p = 0.10), consistent with the original study's findings.

original_authors: Hare, T.; Camerer, C.; Rangel, A.
original_title: Self-control in decision-making involves modulation of the vmPFC valuation system
description: Activity in ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) encodes food value and integrates health and taste attributes during self-control decisions, with dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) modulating vmPFC to incorporate long-term health goals
justification: The authors report mixed replication results across four key hypotheses. They successfully replicated findings about vmPFC value signals (H1-H2), stating "Our data provide further support for the now widely accepted notion that decisions are associated with a value signal in vmPFC." However, they failed to replicate the dlPFC findings, stating "We did not find strong evidence in support of the second set of hypotheses (Hypotheses 3 and 4)...which highlight the role of left dlPFC in self-control." Table 2 in the paper classifies results as: H1 "Supported", H2 "Supported with reservations", H3 "Not supported", and H4 "Mixed evidence".

original_authors: Monteith, S.; Glenn, T.
original_title: A comparison of potential psychiatric drug interactions from six drug interaction database programs
description: Six commercial drug interaction database programs show inconsistent categorization of potential drug-drug interactions for 100 drug pairs involving psychiatric drugs, with overall agreement of only 66%
justification: The replication successfully confirmed the original findings. The authors state: 'After 2 years of updates to all six drug interaction database programs, differences remain in the category of potential DDI for the 100 drug pairs involving psychiatric drugs. Just as in 2018...' The overall percent agreement was 67% in 2020 compared to 66% in 2018, and the Fleiss kappa remained fair (0.266 vs 0.257).

original_authors: Haeffel, G.
original_title: Motion as Motivation: Using Repetitive Flexion Movements to Stimulate the Approach System
description: Repeated finger flexion movements increase approach-reward motivation and persistence on difficult tasks
justification: Results were highly inconsistent across two studies. The authors conclude: "the effects of repeated finger flexion movements on reward motivation, affect, and behavior appear to be inconsistent and weak... there is little evidence that body movements have a reliable and valid causal effect on approach-reward motivation." Each study found one significant effect but on different dependent variables, which the authors attribute to chance findings rather than genuine effects.

original_authors: Chomsky, C.
original_title: The Acquisition of Syntax in Children from 5 to 10
description: Children do not master the syntactic form of sentences like 'John is easy to see' until after age 8 years (approximately 100 months)
justification: The authors found that when visual context was properly controlled, children acquired this syntactic ability by age 67 months (not 100 months as Chomsky claimed), stating "children have acquired the linguistic ability to cope with sentence type (1) at an earlier age than suggested by Chomsky" and "Chomsky's age estimates were distorted upward by the dominating effects of the visual aspects of her task."

original_authors: Conrad, R.; Schilling, G.; Langenbuch, M.
original_title: Alexithymia in male infertility
description: Infertile men show significantly higher levels of alexithymia and somatization compared to healthy controls
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: 'In summary, it can be stated that the hypothesis of increased alexithymia and somatization in infertile men has now been confirmed in 2 studies.' The abstract also clearly states: 'Our study replicated the findings of the previous investigation.' Both main findings (higher alexithymia with p<0.01 and higher somatization with p<0.05) were successfully reproduced.

original_authors: De Souza J; Govaux P; Julien N; Potvin S; Charest J; Marchand S
original_title: Fibromyalgia subgroups: proWling distinct subgroups using the Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire. A preliminary study
description: A classification system divides fibromyalgia patients into two subgroups (Type I and Type II) based on Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire subscale scores, with Type I patients scoring low on morning tiredness, anxiety, and depression, while Type II patients score high on these measures.
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "Our data show that the differentiation of fibromyalgia patients in type I and type II subgroups seems reproducible and reliable" and in the abstract that "The profiles of type I and type II patients from our sample strikingly paralleled those of the original study, demonstrating the reproducibility of the classification."

original_authors: Oberman, L.; Ramachandran, V.
original_title: Preliminary evidence for deficits in multisensory integration in autism spectrum disorders: The mirror neuron hypothesis
description: Individuals with autism spectrum conditions show diminished crossmodal correspondences (the 'kiki/bouba' effect), matching words to shapes based on supramodal characteristics less frequently than neurotypical individuals
justification: The authors explicitly state that 'direct replication of [19] study failed, despite a larger sample size' when using all five stimulus pairs. They report only 'partial confirmation' of the effect when excluding two problematic pairs, concluding 'we partially confirmed the diminished crossmodal correspondences effect' and noting results 'have to be interpreted very cautiously.'

original_authors: Heschl, R.
original_title: Tiefen-Windungen des menschlichen Grosshirns und die Ueberbrückung der Zentralfurche
description: The 'bridged' central sulcus represents an extreme variant of the common 'deep winding' (pli de passage fronto-pariétal moyen) at the same location in the fundus of the central sulcus, with both showing a continuum of heights.
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: 'The present study successfully replicated Heschl's historical survey of the rare "bridged" CS and the heights of the "deep winding"... This successful replication corroborates Heschl's hypothesis that the "deep winding" and the "bridged" CS represent different manifestations of the same anatomical structure.' Both the prevalence rates (0.8% vs 0.6%) and the skewed height distribution were confirmed.

original_authors: Jellinger, K.; Attems, J.
original_title: Does striatal pathology distinguish Parkinson disease with dementia and dementia with Lewy bodies?
description: Striatal β-amyloid deposition differentiates dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) from Parkinson's disease dementia (PDD)
justification: The authors explicitly state in their Discussion: 'we obtained more robust predictive statistics to support the concept published by Professor Jellinger that DLB cases have significantly higher striatal Ab deposition than cases with PDD' and 'Overall our findings strongly support Professor Jellinger's suggestion that differences in striatal Ab load contribute to the timing of dementia relative to Parkinsonism in DLB versus PDD.'

original_authors: Paternoster, R.; Mcgloin, J.; Nguyen, H.; Thomas, K.
original_title: The causal impact of exposure to deviant peers: An experimental investigation
original_journal: Journal of Research in Crime and Delinquency
description: Brief exposure to a deviant peer increases the amount of deviant behavior in young adults
justification: The authors achieved partial replication. In their conclusion they state: "this study replicates the finding that a brief exposure to deviant modeling by a previously unknown peer subsequently increases the amount of deviant behavior in young adults. However, we did not replicate the finding that only participants who were exposed to a deviant peer engaged in deviancy."

original_authors: Laban, G.; Kappas, A.; Morrison, V.; Cross, E.
original_title: Building longterm human-robot relationships: examining disclosure, perception and well-being across time
description: Repeated self-disclosure to a social robot over time increases disclosure behavior, improves social perceptions of the robot as more social and competent, and enhances emotional well-being through improved mood, reduced loneliness, and decreased stress
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'Our results replicated [1] showing that informal caregivers self-disclose increasingly more to a social robot over time... and perceive the robot as more social and competent over time. Furthermore, we found that informal caregivers' moods positively change after interacting with the robot, they also perceive the robot to be more comforting over time, and they feel less lonely and stressed overtime... The present findings replicate our previous result [1], providing compelling evidence for social robots' potential to establish meaningful relationships with human users.'

original_authors: Chen, J.; He, T.; Riyanto, Y.
original_title: The effect of language on economic behavior: Examining the causal link between future tense and time preference in the lab
description: Using future tense (versus present tense) to refer to future events causes less patient behavior in intertemporal choice tasks
justification: The authors state 'We find that consistent with the results by Chen et al. (2019) varying the language use in the instructions does not affect revealed patience' and 'Our results are in line with the findings by Chen et al. and therefore speak against an immediate effect of language structure on intertemporal preferences.' This successfully replicates the original null finding.

original_authors: Lumsden, J.; Miles, L.; Macrae, C.
original_title: Perceptions of synchrony: Different strokes for different folks?
description: Dyads with similar skin tones are perceived to exhibit higher levels of synchrony than dyads with dissimilar skin tones, despite objective coordination levels being equivalent
justification: The authors explicitly state: "Replicating the findings of [45], dyads comprised of individuals with similar skin tones were perceived to exhibit higher levels of synchrony than dyads with dissimilar skin tones, despite an objective equivalence in the level of coordination actually present." The pre-registered replication with a larger sample (n=191 vs n=58) successfully confirmed the original effect.

original_authors: Ward, A.; Duke, K.; Gneezy, A.; Bos, M.
original_title: Brain drain: The mere presence of one's own smartphone reduces available cognitive capacity
original_journal: Journal of the Association for Consumer Research
description: Closer proximity to one's smartphone reduces available cognitive capacity (working memory performance), with this effect being stronger for individuals with higher smartphone attachment and dependency
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "the present study's findings failed to replicate Ward et al.'s main effect concerning performance on the OSpan task... Therefore, the 'brain drain' effect was not replicated in the present study." They found no significant effect of smartphone location on OSpan performance (p = .91), directly contradicting the original finding.

original_authors: Piech, R.; Pastorino, M.; Zald, D.
original_title: All I saw was the cake: Hunger effects on attentional capture by visual food cues
description: Hunger increases attentional capture by food cues (but not other types of cues) in an emotional blink of attention task, producing worse performance on lag2 trials with food distractors when participants are hungry compared to when sated
justification: The authors explicitly state: "We found no evidence for P1 in E1 or E2, instead finding evidence supporting the null... We did not replicate the key finding of interest in PPZ." They conclude: "We did not find a relationship between hunger and the attentional capture of food cues in the present study."

original_authors: Diazgranados, N.; Ibrahim, L.; Brutsche, N.; Newberg, A.; Kronstein, P.; Khalife, S.
original_title: A randomized add-on trial of an N-methyl-D-aspartate antagonist in treatment-resistant bipolar depression
description: A single intravenous infusion of ketamine (0.5 mg/kg) produces rapid (within 1 hour) antidepressant effects in patients with treatment-resistant bipolar depression
justification: The authors explicitly state "This double-blind, placebo-controlled, proof-of-concept study replicated our previous finding that a single intravenous infusion of an NMDA antagonist resulted in a robust and rapid (within 1 hour) antidepressant response in patients with bipolar depression." They note "notable similarities" including similar response rates (64% vs. 56% at 40 minutes) and timing of effects.

original_authors: Calogero, R.; Thompson, J.
original_title: Potential implications of the objectification of women's bodies for women's sexual satisfaction
description: Self-surveillance (a form of self-objectification) directly predicts lower sexual satisfaction and sexual self-esteem in women
justification: The authors explicitly state that "our findings did not support the role of self-surveillance as a direct predictor of sexual satisfaction or sexual self-esteem as reported in previous research" and "The relationships between self-surveillance and sexual self-esteem... and self-surveillance and sexual satisfaction... were not significant in the present study and did not replicate."

original_authors: Jacobs, R.; Watkins, E.; Peters, A.; Feldhaus, C.; Barba, A.; Carbray, J.; Langenecker, S.
original_title: Targeting ruminative thinking in adolescents at risk for depressive relapse: Rumination-focused cognitive behavior therapy in a pilot randomized controlled trial with resting state fMRI
description: Rumination-focused cognitive behavioral therapy reduces depressive rumination and cross-network connectivity between the left posterior cingulate cortex and right inferior frontal/inferior temporal gyri in adolescents with remitted major depressive disorder
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: "the current results included a planned, registered replication of change in reduction of the ruminative habit and cross-network resting-state connectivity." Both primary outcomes were successfully replicated with large effect sizes (z = 0.84 for rumination reduction; z = 0.73 for connectivity reduction).

original_authors: Sharon O; Fahoum F; Nir Y
original_title: Transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation in humans induces pupil dilation and attenuates alpha oscillations
description: Short bursts of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) induce transient pupil dilation and attenuate EEG alpha oscillations, both markers of central noradrenergic activity
justification: The authors successfully replicated the pupil dilation effect ("In accordance with Sharon et al. [31], we found stronger pupil dilation following short bursts of taVNS compared to sham stimulation (BF10 = 7.45)") but failed to replicate the EEG alpha power effect ("We did not replicate the finding of Sharon et al. [31] that short-lasting taVNS transiently attenuated EEG alpha activity; our data were four times more likely under the null hypothesis"). This mixed pattern of results constitutes a partial replication.

original_authors: Sperling, G.
original_title: The information available in brief visual presentations
description: Iconic memory (visual sensory store) has a large capacity but decays within approximately 1000ms after stimulus offset, as measured by the partial report paradigm
justification: The authors explicitly state in their Results section: 'This analysis replicated the original Sperling findings, revealing a significant effect of delay (F(1, 38) = 21.71, p < 0.001, η p 2 = 0.37).' The Discussion confirms: 'In Experiment 1, we directly replicated the original Sperling paradigm using alphanumeric stimuli' and successfully observed the characteristic decay of iconic memory over time.

original_authors: Forstmann, B.; Anwander, A.; Schäfer, A.; Neumann, J.; Brown, S.; Wagenmakers, E.
original_title: Cortico-striatal connections predict control over speed and accuracy in perceptual decision making
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
description: Individual differences in tract strength from right pre-SMA to right striatum predict individual differences in control over speed and accuracy in perceptual decision making
justification: The authors state: 'The Bayes factor shows that there is moderate support for the null hypothesis of no correlation.' The additional exploratory analysis showed 'the data are extremely likely to have occurred under the null hypothesis compared to the proponent's hypothesis.' The p-value indicated a failed replication.

original_authors: Kanai, R.; Bahrami, B.; Roylance, R.; Rees, G.
original_title: Online social network size is reflected in human brain structure
description: Individual differences in online social network size (Facebook friends) and real-world social network size are positively correlated with grey matter volume in brain regions including left middle temporal gyrus, right superior temporal sulcus, right entorhinal cortex, and bilateral amygdala
justification: Mixed results across 6 tested effects: 'In 5 out of 6 cases we find support for the null hypothesis.' However, for the correlation between real-world social network size (SNS) and GM volume in right amygdala, 'the p-value indicates a successful replication.' The Bayes factors showed moderate support for null in 3 effects and ambiguous results in 2 others.

original_authors: Xu, J.; Kober, H.; Carroll, K.; Rounsaville, B.; Pearlson, G.; Potenza, M.
original_title: White matter integrity and behavioral activation in healthy subjects
description: Individual differences in white matter integrity (measured by diffusion tensor imaging) in brain pathways are positively correlated with individual differences in behavioral activation system (BAS) scores measuring reward sensitivity and fun-seeking
justification: The authors report: 'In all cases we find support for the null hypothesis. The Bayes factors show that there is moderate or strong support for the null hypothesis in 3 out of 4 tests.' The exploratory analysis showed 'for three effects there is extreme evidence in favor of the null hypothesis compared to the proponent's hypothesis.' All p-values indicated failed replications.

original_authors: Kanai, R.; Dong, M.; Bahrami, B.; Rees, G.
original_title: Distractibility in daily life is reflected in the structure and function of human parietal cortex
description: Individual differences in distractibility (measured by the Cognitive Failures Questionnaire) are correlated with grey matter volume in left superior parietal lobe (positive correlation) and left middle prefrontal cortex (negative correlation)
justification: The authors found 'In both cases we find anecdotal support for the null hypothesis.' However, they note this is 'not worth more than a bare mention' (quoting Jeffreys). While the exploratory analysis showed anecdotal evidence favoring the proponent's hypothesis, the overall pattern supports a failed replication, consistent with the Discussion stating they 'were unable to successfully replicate any of these 17 correlations.'

original_authors: Westlye, L.; Grydeland, H.; Walhovd, K.; Fjell, A.
original_title: Associations between regional cortical thickness and attentional networks as measured by the attention network test
description: Individual differences in attentional network functioning (executive control and alerting) are negatively correlated with cortical thickness in specific brain regions including left caudal anterior cingulate cortex, left superior temporal gyrus, right middle temporal gyrus, and left superior parietal lobe
justification: The authors report: 'In all cases we find support for the null hypothesis. The Bayes factors show that there is moderate support for the null hypothesis in one out of four tests' with 'ambiguous' results for the other three. All p-values indicated failed replications. The Discussion confirms they 'were unable to successfully replicate any of these 17 correlations.'

original_authors: Dienes, Z.; Hutton, S.
original_title: Understanding hypnosis metacognitively: rTMS applied to left DLPFC increases hypnotic suggestibility
description: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) applied to left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex increases hypnotic suggestibility as measured by subjective ratings
justification: The authors explicitly state: 'Our results differed from theirs: they found that TMS to left DLPFC increased subjective (but not objective) ratings of hypnotizability, whereas we found no effect of such stimulation on either type of measure of hypnotizability.' The replication found no effect on either subjective or objective measures (B < .33 for both).

original_authors: Inzlicht, M.; Al-Khindi, T.
original_title: ERN and the Placebo: A Misattribution Approach to Studying the Arousal Properties of the Error-Related Negativity
description: The error-related negativity (ERN) amplitude is reduced when participants misattribute their arousal to a placebo rather than their task performance
justification: The authors explicitly state they 'subsequently failed to replicate its three principal findings' and that the manipulation check failed. They conclude: 'the present study does provide some evidence against replicability of Inzlicht & Al-Khindi's (2012) misattribution of arousal paradigm' and note findings are 'consistent with the view that our original study may have been a false positive.'

original_authors: Alais, D.; Burr, D.
original_title: The ventriloquist effect results from near-optimal bimodal integration
description: Human observers integrate auditory and visual spatial signals weighted in proportion to their relative sensory reliabilities, conforming to maximum likelihood estimation predictions
justification: The replication showed mixed results: while observers achieved significant variance reduction for audiovisual relative to unisensory conditions in agreement with MLE, they weighted visual signals significantly stronger than predicted by MLE. The authors state "observers integrate audiovisual signals approximately as predicted by MLE. However, the sensory weights deviated significantly from MLE predictions" and conclude that "naive observers do not integrate audiovisual spatial signals in a way that is consistent with the principles of maximum likelihood estimation."

original_authors: Schiller D; Monfils M; Raio C; Johnson D; Ledoux J; Phelps E
original_title: Preventing the return of fear in humans using reconsolidation update mechanisms
description: Conducting extinction training within 10 minutes of memory reactivation (during the reconsolidation window) prevents the later spontaneous recovery and reinstatement of conditioned fear responses
justification: The authors explicitly state: "we observed spontaneous recovery of fear and susceptibility to reinstatement in both the reactivation and no reactivation groups, without any significant between-group differences" and "we could not observe any benefit of reactivation-extinction over regular extinction training in preventing recovery of conditioned fear."

original_authors: May, A.; Burrows, K.; Figueroa-Hall, L.; Kirlic, N.; White, E.; Smith, R.; Ekhtiari, H.; Paulus, M.; Savitz, J.; Stewart, J.
original_title: Sex differences in circulating inflammatory mediators as a function of substance use disorder
description: Females with substance use disorders exhibit lower C-reactive protein (CRP) but higher interleukin-8 (IL-8) and interleukin-10 (IL-10) concentrations than females with mood/anxiety disorders but no SUD
justification: The authors state "One out of the three biomarker findings fully replicated, wherein females with SUD exhibited lower CRP concentrations than females without SUD." However, "regression models for IL-8 and IL-10 did not replicate," though IL-8 showed the expected direction in simple regression. This constitutes a partial replication with mixed results across the three biomarkers.

original_authors: Benowitz, L.; Goldberg, D.; Madsen, J.; Soni, D.; Irwin, N.
original_title: Inosine stimulates extensive axon collateral growth in the rat corticospinal tract after injury
original_journal: Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U S A
description: Intracortical delivery of inosine promotes trans-midline growth of corticospinal tract axons in the spinal cord after unilateral injury to the medullary pyramid
justification: The authors explicitly state in their Discussion: "The present results revealed no evidence that intracortical delivery of inosine triggered extensive growth of CST axons across the astroglial boundary at the midline of the dorsal column following unilateral pyramidotomy, as reported by Benowitz et al." and conclude "The present results fail to confirm the report of Benowitz et al."

original_authors: Sindermann, C.; Kuss, D.; Throuvala, M.; Griffiths, M.; Montag, C.
original_title: Should we pay for our social media/messenger applications? Preliminary data on the acceptance of an alternative to the current prevailing data business model
description: Social media users show willingness to pay monthly fees for digital wellbeing services including better data protection, less marketing use of their data, design that does not prolong usage time, and reduction of fake news and radicalism
justification: The replication successfully confirmed and extended the original findings. The authors state: "participants' interest in paying for social media digital wellbeing features is higher now compared to earlier. Specifically, there is a significant difference in participants' total score of willingness to pay for social media platforms in 2022 compared to 2020" and "The study...found significantly higher scores in participants' willingness to pay for social media and messenger services in 2022."

original_authors: Stevanovic, M.; Himberg, T.; Niinisalo, M.; Kahri, M.; Peräkylä, A.; Sams, M.; Hari, R.
original_title: Sequentiality, mutual visibility, and behavioral matching: Body sway and pitch register during joint decision making
original_journal: Research on Language and Social Interaction
description: Body sway matching is higher during decision-making phases than during search phases in dyadic joint decision-making conversations
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: 'the results of [29] could be replicated in a German-speaking population' and 'With this study we could confirm higher matching of body sway during decision than search phases.' The replication found statistically significant effects (p = 0.043 for WCC, p < 0.001 for COM acceleration) in the same direction as the original study.

original_authors: Kanai, R.; Feilden, T.; Firth, C.; Rees, G.
original_title: Political orientations are correlated with brain structure in young adults
description: Conservatives show larger gray matter volume in the right amygdala compared to liberals
justification: The authors explicitly state they 'preregistered and replicated the finding that amygdala gray matter volume correlatives positively with conservatism' and that 'The current replication study using a fairly large and politically diverse dataset adds partial support to this hypothesis.' Despite a smaller effect size than the original, the replication was statistically significant (p = 0.041) in the expected direction.

original_authors: Kanai, R.; Feilden, T.; Firth, C.; Rees, G.
original_title: Political orientations are correlated with brain structure in young adults
description: Liberals show larger gray matter volume in the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) compared to conservatives
justification: The authors clearly state 'we failed to replicate the negative correlation between conservatism and the ACC' and 'we still fail to replicate this relationship' (p = 0.685). The exploratory and confirmatory data splits did not align, and the authors explicitly rejected the link between social ideology and ACC.

original_authors: Lazarov, A.; Abend, R.; Bar-Haim, Y.
original_title: Social anxiety is related to increased dwell time on socially threatening faces
description: Individuals with social anxiety disorder dwell longer on socially threatening (disgust) faces compared to neutral faces when viewing face matrices, as measured by eye-tracking total dwell time
justification: The authors explicitly state 'The attempt was successful, as results were consistent with the findings from the original study.' The replication found the same significant group-by-AOI interaction effect, with SAD patients dwelling significantly longer on threat faces compared to healthy controls, and results remained significant after controlling for depression.

original_authors: Locke, J.
original_title: Ease of articulation
original_journal: Journal of speech and hearing research
description: Adults can reliably rate the ease of articulation of consonant sounds, and these ease ratings correlate positively with the order in which children acquire speech sounds
justification: The authors explicitly state: "We were able to replicate the results of Locke's experiments, with especially close replication of Experiment 2." Experiment 2 showed a very high positive correlation (rs=.93, p<.000001) described as "nearly perfect," while Experiment 1 showed a moderate positive correlation (rs=.69, p<0.00038).

original_authors: Mussweiler, T.; Englich, B.
original_title: Subliminal anchoring: Judgmental consequences and underlying mechanisms
original_journal: Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes
description: Subliminally presented numeric anchors (without conscious awareness or deliberate processing) bias subsequent numeric estimates toward the anchor value
justification: The authors explicitly state in their general discussion: "In two high-powered, preregistered, close replications, we found no evidence for subliminal anchoring." For Study 1, they report "there was no sign of anchoring-even after we excluded outliers and controlled for whether participants saw the flickering-as inconsistent with the claim that subliminal anchoring exists."

original_authors: Reitsma-Van Rooijen, M.; Daamen, D.; L.
original_title: Subliminal anchoring: The effects of subliminally presented numbers on probability estimates
description: Subliminal anchoring effects occur only when participants are under time pressure to provide their estimates quickly
justification: The authors state in the Study 2 discussion: "In our high-powered, preregistered, close replication of [Reitsma-van Rooijen et al. 2006], we could not replicate the subliminal anchoring effect that they reported for participants who had to provide their estimates quickly." The general discussion confirms: "we found no evidence for subliminal anchoring."

original_authors: Swami, V.; Voracek, M.; Stieger, S.; Tran, U.; Furnham, A.
original_title: Analytic thinking reduces belief in conspiracy theories
description: Priming analytic thinking through a scrambled sentence verbal fluency task reduces belief in conspiracy theories
justification: The authors found no evidence that the scrambled sentence task reduced conspiracy beliefs. They state: "we found no evidence for the hypothesis that priming analytical thinking through either the scrambled sentence task... reduced such beliefs. On the contrary, Bayesian analyses showed moderate-to-strong evidence for the null hypotheses."

original_authors: Swami, V.; Voracek, M.; Stieger, S.; Tran, U.; Furnham, A.
original_title: Analytic thinking reduces belief in conspiracy theories
description: Priming analytic thinking through difficult-to-read (disfluent) fonts reduces belief in conspiracy theories
justification: The authors found no evidence that disfluent fonts reduced conspiracy beliefs. They conclude: "we found no evidence for the hypothesis that priming analytical thinking through... the use of difficult-to-read fonts... reduced such beliefs" and found "moderate-to-strong evidence for the null hypotheses in both studies."

original_authors: Sugasini D; Thomas R; Yalagala P; Tai L; Subbaiah P
original_title: Dietary docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) as lysophosphatidylcholine, but not as free acid, enriches brain DHA and improves memory in adult mice
description: Dietary sn-1 lysophosphatidylcholine-DHA increases brain DHA levels by approximately 100% (relative percent) and up to 200% (concentration) compared to free DHA or control
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "we observed no significant differences in DHA concentration or relative percent in any brain region between control and treatment groups" and "our results do not support the claim that PL-DHA forms significantly increase brain DHA levels under rigorously matched experimental conditions."

original_authors: Sugasini D; Yalagala P; Goggin A; Tai L; Subbaiah P
original_title: Enrichment of brain docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) is highly dependent upon the molecular carrier of dietary DHA: Lysophosphatidylcholine is more efficient than either phosphatidylcholine or triacylglycerol
description: Di-DHA phosphatidylcholine increases brain DHA levels by approximately 35% compared to triacylglycerol-DHA
justification: The authors conclude: "we failed to reproduce the finding by Subbaiah et al. of increased brain DHA upon administration of di-DHA-PC" and "no significant differences in DHA relative percent or concentration were observed between control and treatment groups in any brain region."

original_authors: Rabbitts, J.; Zhou, C.; Groenewald, C.; Durkin, L.; Palermo, T.
original_title: Trajectories of postsurgical pain in children: Risk factors and impact of late pain recovery on long-term health outcomes after major surgery
description: Two distinct postsurgical pain trajectories emerge in adolescents following major surgery: one group experiences declining pain while another experiences high and persistent pain with poorer long-term health outcomes
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'This study replicated results from the prior Rabbitts et al. study in a larger sample of adolescents, finding two post-surgical pain trajectories including one with High and Persistent Pain, with an estimated 1 in 5 chance of experiencing high and persistent pain over the year following major surgery.'

original_authors: Takahashi, H.; Iwase, M.; Ishii, R.; Ohi, K.; Fukumoto, M.; Azechi, M.; Ikezawa, K.; Kurimoto, R.; Canuet, L.; Nakahachi, T.; Iike, N.; Tagami, S.; Morihara, T.; Okochi, M.; Tanaka, T.; Kazui, H.; Yoshida, T.; Tanimukai, H.; Yasuda, Y.; Kudo, T.; Hashimoto, R.; Takeda, M.
original_title: Impaired prepulse inhibition and habituation of acoustic startle response in Japanese patients with schizophrenia
description: Japanese schizophrenic patients show reduced habituation (HAB) and prepulse inhibition (PPI) of the acoustic startle response compared to healthy controls
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: "we were able to replicate the HAB impairment and PPI deficit in chronic Japanese schizophrenic patients" and found significant differences for all startle measures (ASR, HAB, and PPI at 82, 86, and 90 dB) between patients and controls.

original_authors: Monfils, M.; Cowansage, K.; Klann, E.; Ledoux, J.
original_title: Extinction-reconsolidation boundaries: key to persistent attenuation of fear memories
description: A single retrieval trial one hour before extinction training results in persistent attenuation of conditioned fear memory, preventing spontaneous recovery of fear after one month
justification: The authors explicitly state: "Overall, we did not find any evidence for reduced return of fear with the retrieval-extinction procedure, as assessed with spontaneous recovery, reinstatement and renewal... Taken together, we did not reproduce the findings of Monfils and colleagues, even though we copied their procedures as closely as possible."

original_authors: Monfils, M.; Cowansage, K.; Klann, E.; Ledoux, J.
original_title: Extinction-reconsolidation boundaries: key to persistent attenuation of fear memories
description: A single retrieval trial one hour before extinction training prevents reinstatement of conditioned fear memory after exposure to aversive stimuli
justification: The authors found no evidence for the retrieval-extinction effect on reinstatement. They state: "In our hands, both groups showed similar reinstatement of cued fear... our data do not support a significant attenuation of reinstatement in the Ret group as compared with the NoRet group."

original_authors: Monfils, M.; Cowansage, K.; Klann, E.; Ledoux, J.
original_title: Extinction-reconsolidation boundaries: key to persistent attenuation of fear memories
description: A single retrieval trial one hour before extinction training prevents renewal of conditioned fear memory when tested in a different context from extinction
justification: The authors found no evidence for the retrieval-extinction effect on renewal. They state: "Our data do not support an attenuation of spontaneous recovery nor renewal in the Ret group as compared with the NoRet group" and "we were unable to reproduce the recovery-attenuating effect of the retrieval-extinction procedure."

original_authors: Alfei, J.; Monti, F.; Molina, R.; Bueno, V.; Urcelay, A.; G.
original_title: Prediction error and trace dominance determine the fate of fear memories after post-training manipulations
description: Post-reactivation systemic administration of midazolam induces amnesia for contextual fear memories in rats
justification: The authors conclude: "we failed to obtain clear evidence for post-reactivation amnesia using systemic administration of drugs." Even in the two experiments (JA11, JA12) performed in the same lab as the original studies that showed marginal statistical significance with one-sided tests, "the obtained effect sizes are markedly smaller than those reported in published studies" and two-sided tests (as used in originals) were non-significant (p=.096, p=.074).

original_authors: Ferrer Monti, R.; Alfei, J.; Mugnaini, M.; Bueno, A.; Beckers, T.; Urcelay, G.; Molina, V.
original_title: A comparison of behavioral and pharmacological interventions to attenuate reactivated fear memories
description: Post-reactivation systemic administration of midazolam induces amnesia for contextual fear memories in rats
justification: Multiple exact replication attempts failed. The authors state: "we obtained no evidence for the induction of amnesia by post-reactivation MDZ administration, despite following the methodology of previous, successful studies as precisely as possible." Even in experiments JA11 and JA12 that showed marginal effects, "the obtained effect sizes were smaller than those reported in prior publications."

original_authors: Stern, C.; Gazarini, L.; Takahashi, R.; Guimarães, F.; Bertoglio, L.
original_title: On disruption of fear memory by reconsolidation blockade: Evidence from cannabidiol treatment
description: Post-reactivation systemic administration of midazolam induces amnesia for contextual fear memories in rats
justification: In experiment NS11, an exact replication of Stern et al. (2012), "visual inspection of the graphs shows that SAL rats showed lower freezing at test compared to MDZ rats, a pattern opposite to the findings reported in the original paper." Statistical tests provided "no evidence for an amnestic effect of MDZ" with Bayesian analysis suggesting "anecdotal evidence for the absence of an amnestic effect."

original_authors: De Leon, J.; Diaz, F.; Rogers, T.; Browne, D.; Dinsmore, L.
original_title: Initiation of daily smoking and nicotine dependence in schizophrenia and mood disorders
description: Schizophrenia vulnerability is associated with higher risk of initiating daily smoking after 20 years of age
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion that "The above conclusions are consistent with those from the previous US study [3]" and in the Conclusion that "This Spanish replication of US results suggests that vulnerability to schizophrenia may be associated with a higher risk of becoming a daily smoker." The replication found significantly different cumulative hazard curves (p<0.001) with higher smoking initiation rates after age 20 in schizophrenia patients, consistent with the original US findings.

original_authors: Boayue, N.; Csifcsák, G.; Kreis, I.; Schmidt, C.; Finn, I.; Hovde Vollsund, A.; Mittner, M.
original_title: The interplay between executive control, behavioural variability and mind wandering: insights from a high-definition transcranial direct-current stimulation study
description: High-definition transcranial direct current stimulation (HD-tDCS) over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex reduces mind wandering propensity during a finger-tapping random sequence generation task
justification: The authors explicitly state: "we did not find any effect on the propensity to mind wander in the real relative to the sham stimulation group during the stimulation block" and conclude that "the earlier finding by [8] was most likely a statistical fluke." When combining their data with the original study (N=160), "the combined analysis also failed to show an effect of HD-tDCS on the propensity to MW."

original_authors: Ulrich M; Keller J; Grön G
original_title: Neural signatures of experimentally induced flow experiences identified in a typical fMRI block design with BOLD imaging
description: During experimentally induced flow states, an inverted U-shaped pattern of neural activation occurs, with greater activation during flow compared to boredom and overload conditions in brain regions including dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, anterior insula, and parietal cortex
justification: The authors report 'decisive evidence for the replication' of the inverted U-shaped flow effect with replication Bayes factors above 300. In the Conclusion, they state 'both major flow effects on neural activation could be very well replicated.'

original_authors: Ulrich M; Keller J; Grön G
original_title: Neural signatures of experimentally induced flow experiences identified in a typical fMRI block design with BOLD imaging
description: During experimentally induced flow states, a U-shaped pattern of neural activation occurs, with lower activation during flow compared to boredom and overload conditions in brain regions including medial prefrontal cortex, ventral striatum, amygdala, and cingulate cortex
justification: The authors report 'decisive evidence for the replication' of the U-shaped flow effect with replication Bayes factors above 300. In the Conclusion, they state 'both major flow effects on neural activation could be very well replicated.'

original_authors: Schwabe, L.; Wolf, O.
original_title: Stress prompts habit behavior in humans
description: Acute stress exposure before instrumental learning causes participants to become insensitive to outcome devaluation, leading to more habitual (rather than goal-directed) responding
justification: The authors explicitly state: "In contrast to our hypotheses, the results of both experiments failed to provide evidence that acute stress prompts habitual behavior, with additional Bayesian analyses providing substantial evidence for the null hypotheses." They conclude: "We failed to replicate the findings from the original studies."

original_authors: Schwabe, L.; Wolf, O.
original_title: Socially evaluated cold pressor stress after instrumental learning favors habits over goal-directed action
description: Acute stress exposure after instrumental learning and outcome devaluation leads to more habitual responses during extinction testing
justification: The authors state: "the stress and no-stress groups responded indifferently to valued and devalued outcomes" and "We failed to replicate the original pattern of results." The replication found no evidence that stress induced habitual behavior control, with Bayesian analyses supporting the null hypothesis.

original_authors: Anderson, J.; Rungtusanatham, M.; Schroeder, R.; Devaraj, S.
original_title: A path analytic model of a theory of quality management underlying the Deming management method
description: Visionary leadership enables organizational cooperation and learning, which facilitate process management practices, which in turn result in continuous improvement and employee fulfillment, ultimately leading to customer satisfaction
justification: Only Proposition 1 received full empirical support, whereas the remaining three propositions received mixed empirical support. The authors state 'consistent empirical support for four of the eight hypothesized paths can be observed between the U.S. sample and the Italian sample,' indicating partial replication success.

original_authors: Van Dael, F.; Versmissen, D.; Janssen, I.; Myin-Germeys, I.; Van Os, J.; Krabbendam, L.
original_title: Data gathering: Biased in psychosis?
description: JTC (jumping to conclusions) bias is associated with familial liability for psychosis, particularly in siblings of patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorder, and this association is contingent on the presence of delusional ideation
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'The results replicate earlier findings from the study by [Van Dael et al. 2006], in which JTC bias was similarly found to be associated with psychosis liability... and in which a similar interaction was observed between psychosis liability and evidence of delusional ideation.' The conclusion further confirms: 'these findings replicate earlier findings that JTC bias is associated with familial liability for psychosis and that this is contingent on the degree of delusional ideation.'

original_authors: Łodzikowski, K.
original_title: Association between allophonic transcription tool use and phonological awareness level
description: Use of an allophonic transcription tool is associated with increased phonological awareness in Polish learners of English
justification: The authors state 'the results were reproducible but not successful' and conclude that 'to a certain extent, we recreated the results of the original study,' but emphasize that 'results in the original study should be read cautiously and as those of an exploratory study' due to sample size limitations and multicollinearity issues. This represents qualified, limited support rather than clear success or failure.

original_authors: Wadsworth, S.; DeFries, J.; Willcutt, E.; Pennington, B.; Olson, R.
original_title: The Colorado Longitudinal Twin Study of Reading Difficulties and ADHD: Etiologies of Comorbidity and Stability
description: Genetic influences account for more than 60% of reading deficits at initial assessment and substantially influence the stability of reading difficulties over time, with genetic factors also mediating the comorbidity between reading difficulties and ADHD inattention symptoms
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: "Our previous findings of substantial genetic influences for reading deficits and their longitudinal stability are clearly replicated in this independent analysis of twin data." They report that "the overall pattern of results, and indeed most estimates, are highly similar" between the original CLDRC study and the replication ILTS study.

original_authors: Ihme, T.; Tausendpfund, M.
original_title: Gender Differences in Political Knowledge: Bringing Situation Back In
description: Activation of negative gender stereotypes reduces women's performance on political knowledge tests and eliminates the gender gap in political knowledge
justification: The authors explicitly state: "we find no evidence that activation of gender stereotypes affects participants' performance in a political knowledge test. Indeed, we find evidence of absence of this effect." Both Stage 1 (N=671) and Stage 2 (pooled N=1,502) failed to replicate the stereotype activation effect, and Bayesian analyses strongly favored the null hypothesis (replication BF = 0.007, meaning data are 143 times better predicted by the null than the original effect).

original_authors: Tremblay, S.; Jones, D.
original_title: Change of intensity fails to produce an irrelevant sound effect: Implications for the representation of unattended sound
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance
description: The changing-state effect (increased disruption of serial recall by changing-state sequences relative to steady-state sequences) is independent of the intensity at which auditory distractors are presented
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "we replicated the finding that the increased disruption by changing-state relative to steady-state sequences (i.e., the changing-state effect) is independent of intensity" and conclude "we have successfully replicated that the increased disruption by changing-state relative to steady-state sequences is independent of the intensity."

original_authors: Parker, E.; Morihisa, J.; Wyatt, R.; Schwartz, B.; Weingartner, H.; Stillman, R.
original_title: The alcohol facilitation effect on memory: A dose-response study
description: Alcohol consumption following learning enhances performance on a delayed subsequent memory test (retrograde facilitation effect)
justification: The authors report mixed results: "we failed to replicate the original finding by [39] using conventional measures of memory performance (i.e., cued and free recall), we did find clear-cut evidence in favor of an underlying retrieval benefit." They conclude that "our mixed pattern of results best resonates with the idea that alcohol-induced retrograde facilitation really exists but is limited to a retrieval benefit."

original_authors: Bargh, J.; Chaiken, S.; Raymond, P.; Hymes, C.
original_title: The automatic evaluation effect: Unconditional automatic attitude activation with a pronunciation task
original_journal: Behavior Research Methods, Instruments, and Computers
description: Valenced target words are pronounced faster after presentation of an affectively related prime word than after an affectively unrelated prime word, demonstrating goal-independent automatic attitude activation
justification: The authors explicitly state "we failed to obtain significant affective priming of pronunciation responses" and note that "the crucial interaction between prime valence and target valence failed to reach significance, F(1, 43) = 1.95, p > .17." They conclude this is a "statistically reliable null finding" with power > .995 that "seriously questions the reliability of the affective priming effect in the pronunciation task."

original_authors: Beach, S. R. H.; Amir, N.
original_title: Is depression taxonic, dimensional, or both
description: Involuntary defeat syndrome (IDS), as measured by six somatic Beck Depression Inventory items, represents a small latent taxon (a categorical depressive subtype) rather than a dimensional construct
justification: The authors state: "The present results closely mirrored those obtained by Beach and Amir, but parallel analysis of simulated comparison data clearly revealed these results to be more indicative of dimensional than taxonic structure. Further replication within a clinical sample... similarly refuted Beach and Amir's original taxonic interpretation of IDS."

original_authors: Fernandez-Duque, D.; Knight, M.
original_title: Cognitive control: Dynamic, sustained, and voluntary influences
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance
description: A cue predicting conflict in an upcoming flanker task modulates conflict regulation in a subsequent number Stroop task, demonstrating across-task anticipatory cognitive control.
justification: The authors explicitly state in the General Discussion: "We found no evidence for a carry-over effect of anticipatory cognitive control. In all three experiments, the size of the number congruency effect was statistically identical for cues that signaled hard flanker trials and cues that signaled easy flanker trials."

original_authors: Walters, G.
original_title: Dementia: Continuum or distinct entity?
description: Dementia has a dimensional (continuous) rather than categorical latent structure
justification: The replication found the opposite result from the original study. The authors state: "In contrast to the findings reported by Walters (2010), who found evidence to suggest that the construct of dementia is best conceptualized as a continuous variable, our replication of these analyses supports the notion that dementia is a discrete categorical entity" (CCFI values of .751 vs Walters' .245).

original_authors: Jiang, N.; Forster, K.
original_title: Cross-language priming asymmetries in lexical decision and episodic recognition
description: Masked translation priming from L2 (English) to L1 (Chinese) occurs in episodic recognition tasks for studied words but not in lexical decision tasks
justification: The authors explicitly state that 'the most critical of the Jiang and Forster (2001) findings was replicated; L2-L1 priming was found for the old items but not for the new items in an episodic recognition task, and no priming was obtained in a lexical decision task.'

original_authors: Campbell, J.; Phenix, T.
original_title: Target strength and retrieval-induced forgetting in semantic recall
description: A single retrieval of unpracticed multiplication problems produces much larger retrieval-induced forgetting (RIF) of their addition counterparts compared to many retrieval-practice trials (hyper-RIF effect, approximately 200% greater RIF)
justification: The authors explicitly state: "Most important in the present context, neither group presented evidence of the hyper-RIF effect reported by Campbell and Phenix (2009)" and "The present failure to observe hyper-RIF in arithmetic memory aligns with the previous failures of Experiment 1 to replicate the effect." Two experiments failed to replicate the hyper-RIF phenomenon despite careful attempts to recreate the original conditions.

original_authors: Pizzagalli D; Jahn A; Shea O; J
original_title: Toward an objective characterization of an anhedonic phenotype: A signal-detection approach
description: Depression and melancholic symptoms are negatively associated with reward sensitivity (response bias) in a probabilistic reward task
justification: The authors explicitly state: "we found no associations between response-bias variables and BDI and replicated none of the significant effects from the original study" and conclude that "these null findings suggest that the original results may have been false positives."

original_authors: Shariff, A.; Norenzayan, A.
original_title: God is watching you: Priming God concepts increases prosocial behavior in an anonymous economic game
description: Religious priming via scrambled sentence tasks containing religious words increases generosity in anonymous dictator game allocations.
justification: The authors explicitly state they "did not find a statistically significant effect for religious priming" and "were unable to reproduce the positive significant effect of religious priming on generosity in dictator games that Shariff & Norenzayan discovered." All statistical comparisons were nonsignificant (p = .53, .56, .24).

original_authors: Kühnen, U.; Oyserman, D.
original_title: Thinking about the self influences thinking in general: Cognitive consequences of salient self-concept
description: Priming a collectivistic social orientation (compared with an individualistic one) boosts object-location memory
justification: The authors conclude in the General Discussion: "social orientation priming had little influence on memory" and "Any effects of social orientation priming on object-location memory are likely smaller than previously thought." Across four well-powered experiments, they found no significant priming effects on memory, even with an exact replication in Experiment 4.

original_authors: Oyserman, D.; Sorensen, N.; Reber, R.; Chen, S.
original_title: Connecting and separating mind-sets: Culture as situated cognition
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
description: Priming a collectivistic social orientation (compared with an individualistic one) boosts object-location memory
justification: The authors conclude in the General Discussion: "social orientation priming had little influence on memory" and "Any effects of social orientation priming on object-location memory are likely smaller than previously thought." Across four well-powered experiments, they found no significant priming effects on memory, even with an exact replication in Experiment 4.

original_authors: Wansink, B.; Painter, J.; North, J.
original_title: Bottomless bowls: Why visual cues of portion size may influence intake
description: Visual cues of portion size influence food intake, such that people eating from imperceptibly self-refilling bowls consume more soup than those eating from normal bowls without perceiving differences in consumption or satiation
justification: The authors explicitly state in their Discussion: 'The results of the present study did replicate the key finding from Wansink et al.' and 'We therefore deem this replication successful.' The main effect replicated with statistical significance (d = 0.45, which exceeded their preregistered threshold of d = 0.42 for success), showing participants in self-refilling bowls consumed 32% more soup than controls.

original_authors: Gerlicher, A.; Tüscher, O.; Kalisch, R.
original_title: L-DOPA improves extinction memory retrieval after successful fear extinction
description: Post-extinction L-DOPA administration improves extinction memory retrieval 24 hours later, increases spontaneous post-extinction vmPFC reactivations, and this mediates the effect of L-DOPA on extinction memory retrieval
justification: Only 1 of 3 preregistered hypotheses was confirmed: vmPFC reactivations predicted extinction retrieval, but at 90 min rather than 45 min as in the original. The primary hypothesis—that L-DOPA improves extinction retrieval—was not confirmed in preregistered analyses. The authors state: "We could not replicate the facilitating effect of L-DOPA on extinction retrieval (hypothesis 1) and on the number of vmPFC reactivations (hypothesis 3)." Non-preregistered analyses found L-DOPA effects only when controlling for trait salivary alpha-amylase.

original_authors: Oxley, D.
original_title: Political Attitudes Vary with Physiological Traits
description: Conservatives have stronger physiological responses to threatening stimuli than liberals
justification: The authors explicitly state "We, reluctantly, reject the foundational assumption of Oxley et al.'s work." They found no statistically significant association between skin conductance response and social conservatism (b=.01, p=.62), with their standardized coefficient being 37 times smaller than the original effect. Bayes factors provided moderate to strong evidence in favor of the null hypothesis across multiple samples and 16 robustness checks.

original_authors: Kosfeld, M.; Heinrichs, M.; Zak, P.; Fischbacher, U.; Fehr, E.
original_title: Oxytocin increases trust in humans
description: Intranasal oxytocin administration increases investors' willingness to trust in a dyadic economic game with real monetary stakes
justification: The authors explicitly state: "our preregistered analyses show that the simple and general hypothesis that 'OT increases trust' can no longer be endorsed." All three a priori hypotheses were not supported (p=0.745, p=0.259, p=0.091), and Bayesian analyses favored the null hypothesis.

original_authors: Sevenster, D.; Beckers, T.; Kindt, M.
original_title: Prediction error demarcates the transition from retrieval, to reconsolidation, to new learning
description: A single prediction error during memory reactivation followed by propranolol administration triggers memory reconsolidation and reduces fear retention
justification: The authors found no evidence for the expected reconsolidation effect in the single PE group, but state "a straightforward interpretation of these results is complicated by the lack of differential fear retention in the control groups" and "the conclusions that we can draw from the current results are limited." The lack of baseline differential responding prevents definitive interpretation of whether the manipulation failed.

original_authors: Triplett, N.
original_title: The dynamogenic factors in pacemaking and competition
description: Completing a task in competition with another participant leads to improved performance compared to completing the task alone (social facilitation effect)
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: "We replicated the original findings presented by Triplett and provide further evidence for social facilitation and/or competitive coaction effects." In line with Triplett's original study, participants were significantly faster in the together condition than in the alone condition (p < 0.001), and this effect remained robust even when controlling for practice effects, age, and gender.

original_authors: Côté, S.; Piff, P.; Willer, R.
original_title: For whom do the ends justify the means? Social class and utilitarian moral judgment
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
description: High social class individuals are more likely to use utilitarian moral judgment (choosing actions that benefit the most people at the cost of a few), and this association is reduced when empathy is elicited for the disadvantaged
justification: The authors explicitly state "While the results are inconclusive" and describe the findings as "mixed." The first replication (n=226) failed to find the hypothesized interaction effect, while the second replication (n=295) successfully replicated it. The meta-analysis across all three studies (original + two replications) suggested the effect exists but is smaller than originally reported.

original_authors: Mogan, J.; Knox, J. E.
original_title: Characteristics of 'best' and 'worst' clinical teachers as perceived by university nursing faculty and students
description: The 'best' clinical nursing teachers are good role models who enjoy nursing and teaching, demonstrate clinical skill and judgement, and encourage a climate of mutual respect, while 'worst' teachers lack these characteristics.
justification: The authors explicitly state that 'These findings agree with those of Mogan & Knox (1987)' and demonstrate that the most distinguishing characteristics between 'best' and 'worst' clinical teachers (being a good role model and encouraging mutual respect) were consistent with the original study across all measures.

original_authors: Shu, L.; Mazar, N.; Gino, F.; Ariely, D.; Bazerman, M.
original_title: Signing at the beginning makes ethics salient and decreases dishonest self-reports in comparison to signing at the end
description: Signing a veracity statement at the beginning (versus the end) of a self-report form decreases dishonest reporting by making ethics more salient
justification: The authors explicitly state: "we conducted one preregistered, high-powered direct replication of experiment 1 of the PNAS paper, in which we failed to replicate the original result." They found no significant effect on any of the three preregistered outcomes (percent cheating, amount of cheating, expenses reported), with Bayes factors providing substantial support for the null hypothesis.

original_authors: Muir, B.; Moray, N.
original_title: Experimental Studies of Trust and Human Intervention in a Process Control Simulation
description: Trust in automated machines develops through three stages in a specific order: initially from faith, then dependability, and finally predictability
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: 'This study showed that human-machine trust develops differently from the order suggested by [Muir & Moray 1996]' and 'the obtained data patterns were inconsistent with those reported in Muir and Moray.' Instead of faith governing initial trust, the replication found dependability was consistently the dominant dimension at all time points.

original_authors: Hartmann, E.; Sunde, T.; Kristensen, W.; Martinussen, M.
original_title: Psychological measures as predictors of military training performance
description: Rorschach variables measuring stress tolerance, reality testing, and deviant cognition predict pass-fail outcomes in Norwegian Naval Special Forces training, while Big Five personality scales do not predict training outcomes
justification: The authors explicitly state in their discussion: 'This study confirms and strengthens the conclusion from the index study that Rorschach variables are valid predictors of military training performance.' They found the same four Rorschach variables (m, XA%, X-%, and WSum6-Lv2) were significant predictors as in the original study, and like the original, Big Five scales showed no significant correlations.

original_authors: Duff, M.; Gupta, R.; Hengst, J.; Tranel, D.; Cohen, N.
original_title: The use of definite references signals declarative memory: Evidence from hippocampal amnesia
description: Individuals with hippocampal amnesia use significantly fewer definite references when directing in a collaborative barrier task compared to healthy controls
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion that "the difference between amnesia and comparison pairs in the use of indefinite references observed in Duff et al. (in press) was not limited to the productions of the amnesia participants but also extended to their partners," confirming their hypothesis about the distributed impact of memory impairment on definite referencing.

original_authors: Feeney, T.; Ylvisaker, M.
original_title: Context-sensitive behavioral supports for young children with TBI: Short-term effects and long-term outcome
description: Multi-component cognitive-behavioral intervention combining positive behavior supports, cognitive supports, and executive function routines reduces challenging behaviors and increases academic productivity in young children with traumatic brain injury
justification: The authors explicitly state: 'The study was intended as a replication of Feeney and Ylvisaker's [14] single-subject experiments with similarly aged children reported in 2003. As with the 2003 study, hypotheses 1 (that the challenging behaviours would decrease in frequency), 2 (that they would decrease in intensity) and 3 (that amount of work completed would increase) were confirmed for both children.'

original_authors: Jefferies, L.; Smilek, D.; Eich, E.; Enns, J.
original_title: Emotional valence and arousal interact in attentional control
description: Emotional valence and arousal interact to affect attentional control on the Attentional Blink task, with sad mood (low arousal, negative valence) producing best performance and anxious mood (high arousal, negative valence) producing worst performance
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "My confirmatory analyses did not reveal the same effects as those reported by Jefferies et al. Most importantly, I could not replicate the interaction effect of valence and arousal on the difference between T1 and T2 performance for Lag 2 and Lag 4." The crucial interaction did not reach significance (F(2, 143) = .38, p = .54).

original_authors: Bayliss, A.; Paul, M.; Cannon, P.; Tipper, S.
original_title: Gaze cuing and affective judgments of objects: I like what you look at
description: People rate objects as more likeable when they have seen a person repeatedly gaze toward rather than away from those objects (the gaze-liking effect)
justification: Using a large sample (N=98), the replication found essentially no gaze-liking effect (dz = 0.02, 95% CrI [-0.08, 0.10], p = 0.48) compared to the original large effect (dz = 0.94). The authors state: "our results indicate that the effect is very small" and that future researchers would need "at least 3000 participants to detect the gaze-liking effect."

original_authors: Gabrielsson, A.; Juslin, P.
original_title: Emotional expression in music performance: Between the performers's intention and the listener's experience
description: Professional musicians can communicate intended emotional expressions in music to listeners with high decoding accuracy.
justification: The authors explicitly state that "the present study generally supports the findings from Gabrielsson and Juslin (1996)" and found "similarly, high decoding accuracies" with 4 out of 7 emotions (57%) receiving highest average ratings when analyzed using the original methodology, consistent with the original study's findings.

original_authors: Suchotzki, K.; Gamer, M.
original_title: The language of lies: Behavioral and autonomic costs of lying in a native compared to a foreign language
description: Lie-truth differences in response times are smaller when speakers use a foreign language compared to their native language
justification: The authors state that "the subjective estimate of all members of the replication team was that the results replicated the original effect" and conclude "the replication study...also found that speaking in another language reduces the lie-truth difference in RTs," despite noting the effect size was smaller than the original.

original_authors: Johnson, H. C.; Renaud, E. F.; Schmidt, D.; Stanek, E.
original_title: Social worker's views of parents of children with mental and emotional disabilities
original_journal: Families in Society: The Journal of Contemporary Human Services
description: Social workers' beliefs about parents of children with mental and emotional disabilities, measured by the PBAP instrument, cluster into five distinct factors (blame, inform, validate, medicate, instruct), with approximately half of social workers holding parent-blaming beliefs
justification: The authors explicitly state: 'This failure to replicate the Johnson, Renaud, Schmidt and Stanek (1998) results from their study came as a surprise... it proved impossible to confirm the validity of this instrument' for the Australian population. The Australian data did not support the five-factor solution found in the US study.

original_authors: Buffardi, K.
original_title: Assessing individual contributions to software engineering projects with Git Logs and user stories
original_journal: Proceedings of the 51st ACM technical symposium on computer science education
description: Objective metrics from GitHub (commits, line changes, issues) show weak correlations with subjective assessments (peer evaluations and instructor grades) of individual student contributions in team software development projects
justification: The authors explicitly state: "Our study replicated most of Buffardi's key results" and "While replicating all but one of Buffardi's significant findings, our study detected ten of 16 possible significant positive correlations between objective and subjective measures." They successfully replicated 4 out of 5 of Buffardi's main statistical findings.

original_authors: Green, P.
original_title: Comparison between the Test of Memory Malingering (TOMM) and the Nonverbal Symptom Validity Test (NV-MSVT) in adults with disability claims
description: The Nonverbal Medical Symptom Validity Test (NV-MSVT) has superior sensitivity to detecting suboptimal effort and malingering compared to the Test of Memory Malingering (TOMM) in adults with disability claims
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion section: 'In the current study... [Green's] data were very closely replicated. As with the [Green] study, more than twice as many patients failed the NV-MSVT compared with the TOMM.' The abstract confirms: 'results closely matched those of the Green (in press) study.'

original_authors: Rynes, S.; Colbert, A.; Brown, K.
original_title: HR Professionals' Beliefs about Effective Human Resource Practices: Correspondence Between Research and Practice
description: HR professionals' beliefs about effective human resource practices show large discrepancies from research findings, with particularly poor knowledge in recruitment and selection domains
justification: The authors explicitly state in their Discussion: 'In line with the [11] study... in a Dutch sample we found a large gap between practice... and the results of academic research as well. This holds both for the general conclusion and for the differences between the distinguished content areas.' They report 'remarkable similarities' between the American and Dutch samples across multiple dimensions.

original_authors: Owen, J.; Adelson, J.; Budge, S.; Wampold, B.; Kopta, M.; Minami, T.; Miller, S.
original_title: Trajectories of change in psychotherapy
description: Psychotherapy clients follow distinct trajectory patterns during treatment, with three classes identified: Early and Late Change (75%), Slow and Steady (19%), and Worse before Better (5%)
justification: The authors state "We did not exactly replicate the Owen et al. (2015) study" - finding 2 classes instead of 3 - but also note that "distinct subgroups roughly matched two of the three trajectories identified in the original study," providing partial support for multiple change trajectories in psychotherapy.

original_authors: Habota, T.; Mclennan, S.; Cameron, J.; Henry, J.; Ski, C.; Thompson, D.; Rendell, P.
original_title: Prospective memory impairment in chronic heart failure
original_journal: Journal of the International Neuropsychological Society
description: Patients with chronic heart failure show significant prospective memory impairments compared to healthy controls across all types of PM tasks (event-based, time-based, regular, and irregular).
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "Using a different and larger sample, this replication of [9] found that patients with HF had significant and similar sized deficits on all task parameters assessed (event, time, regular, irregular)" and "Our findings are consistent with [9]."

original_authors: Jones, M.; Onslow, M.; Harrison, E.; Packman, A.
original_title: Treating stuttering in young children: Predicting treatment time in the Lidcombe Program
original_journal: Journal of Speech Language and Hearing Research
description: Stuttering severity (percent syllables stuttered) at first clinic visit predicts treatment time with the Lidcombe Program in preschool-age children
justification: The authors explicitly state: 'The present results replicate the findings of Jones et al. (2000)' and 'stuttering rate (%SS) at the first clinic visit is a highly significant predictor of number of clinic visits taken to complete Stage 1.' The replication confirmed the original finding with a British cohort (p=0.029), and meta-analysis of combined data yielded p<0.0001.

original_authors: Marcora, S.; Staiano, W.; Manning, V.
original_title: Mental fatigue impairs physical performance in humans
description: Mental fatigue induced by a demanding cognitive task (90-minute AX-CPT) causes participants to reach exhaustion sooner in a cycling time-to-exhaustion test at 80% peak power output
justification: The authors state in the Discussion: 'Our results are in contrast with those of [Marcora et al. 2009] and add to the growing number of studies failing to find any effects of mental fatigue on physical performance.'
