Despite successfully inducing mental fatigue (BF01 = 0.009), they found moderate-to-strong evidence for the null hypothesis of no effect on time-to-exhaustion performance (BF01 = 9.762).

original_authors: Schlosser, R.; Blischak, D.; Belfiore, P.; Bartley, C.; Barnett, N.
original_title: Effects of synthetic speech output and orthographic feedback on spelling in a student with autism: A preliminary study
description: Speech feedback from a speech-generating device is the most efficient condition for teaching spelling to children with autism compared to print feedback or combined speech-print feedback
justification: The authors explicitly state 'The findings from the above study [19] did not replicate' and found the opposite pattern: PRINT condition was most efficient for their participant with cerebral palsy, whereas the original study found SPEECH was most efficient for a child with autism. The authors discuss this as evidence of different learning profiles between the populations.

original_authors: Schuldt, J.; Rickard, L.; Yang, Z.
original_title: Does reduced psychological distance increase climate engagement? On the limits of localizing climate change
description: Reducing spatial psychological distance through visual cues increases concrete mental construal and affects climate change engagement
justification: The authors report mixed results: the distance manipulation check succeeded, but they explicitly state 'inconsistent with [32], construal level...did not vary significantly across the cued distance conditions.' They conclude 'the evidence presented in both studies suggests that further attempts at replication are necessary.' The core theoretical mechanism (construal level mediating distance effects) failed to replicate, though some moderation effects were observed.

original_authors: Haushofer, J.; Shapiro, J.
original_title: The Short-Term Impact of Unconditional Cash Transfers to the Poor: Evidence from Kenya
description: Unconditional cash transfers increase assets, consumption, revenue, food security, and psychological well-being in poor households in rural Kenya, with no effects on health, education, or female empowerment.
justification: The authors explicitly state: "The replication study findings are consistent with the findings on the short-term impact of the UCT in Kenya as reported in the original study" and "Our study replicates these main findings reported in the original paper, validating the short-term impact of UCT in these different areas in Kenya." The replication reproduced nearly all main results through multiple methods including push-button replication, pure replication, and extensive robustness checks.

original_authors: Folke, S.; Nielsen, A.; Andersen, S.; Karatzias, T.; Karstoft, K.
original_title: ICD-11 PTSD and complex PTSD in treatment-seeking Danish veterans: A latent profile analysis
description: Latent Profile Analysis using the International Trauma Questionnaire identifies distinct classes of individuals with symptom profiles consistent with ICD-11 PTSD and Complex PTSD in treatment-seeking veterans
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: 'Using the ITQ, we replicated findings from our previous LPA study of treatment-seeking veterans identifying two distinct classes of individuals with symptom profiles consistent with the ICD-11 PTSD and CPTSD.' The discussion notes 'The four identified classes in this study clearly mirror four of the classes of [5] and hence, it replicates the finding of a PTSD-class, a CPTSD-class, a DSO-class, and a low symptoms-class.'

original_authors: Burton, J.; Harris, A.; Shah, P.; Hahn, U.
original_title: Optimism where there is none: Asymmetric belief updating observed with valence-neutral life events
description: Individuals update beliefs to a greater extent when learning an event is less likely compared to more likely than expected, even for neutral (non-valenced) events
justification: The authors explicitly state: "we failed to replicate Burton et al.'s (2022) findings of belief update bias for neutral events" and "A belief update bias for neutral events is not observed." Multiple analytic approaches found no difference in updating as a function of whether information was better or worse than expected.

original_authors: Kay, A.; Gaucher, D.; Napier, J.; Callan, M.; Laurin, K.
original_title: God and the government: Testing a compensatory control mechanism for the support of external systems
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
description: Threat to personal control increases endorsement of belief in the existence of a controlling God
justification: The authors state in their Discussion: 'Our results indicate moderate to strong evidence for the absence of this effect: belief in (a controlling) God is not modulated by a threat compared to an affirmation of personal control. Using large samples (N ≈ 400) we did not replicate the original experiment by Kay et al. (2008) in the Netherlands, nor in the US.' They explicitly refer to this as a 'replication failure.'

original_authors: Bargh, J.; Chaiken, S.; Raymond, P.; Hymes, C.
original_title: The automatic evaluation effect: Unconditional automatic attitude activation with a pronunciation task
description: Evaluatively congruent prime-target pairs (e.g., positive prime with positive target) lead to faster pronunciation latencies in a naming task compared to incongruent pairs, reflecting automatic attitude activation
justification: The authors explicitly state: "In five large studies, the effect was not obtained. These results contrast sharply with the repeated successful demonstrations reported in three experiments by Bargh et al." and "Experiment 3 replicated Bargh et al. Experiment 2 as closely as possible. Still, no affective priming effect was observed."

original_authors: He, J.; Gu, D.; Chen, J.; Jaquish, C.; Rao, D.; Hixson, J.; Chen, J.; Duan, X.; Huang, J.; Chen, C.; Kelly, T.; Bazzano, L.; Whelton, P.
original_title: Gender difference in blood pressure responses to dietary sodium intervention in the GenSalt study
description: Blood pressure responses to dietary sodium interventions (low sodium, high sodium) vary greatly among individuals
justification: The authors explicitly state in the conclusion: 'the GenSalt replication study confirmed the large variations of BP responses to dietary sodium and potassium interventions and the CPT among individuals.' They also note the replication study 'provided further evidence to support several observations derived from the GenSalt study.'

original_authors: He, J.; Gu, D.; Chen, J.; Jaquish, C.; Rao, D.; Hixson, J.; Chen, J.; Duan, X.; Huang, J.; Chen, C.; Kelly, T.; Bazzano, L.; Whelton, P.
original_title: Gender difference in blood pressure responses to dietary sodium intervention in the GenSalt study
description: Blood pressure responses to dietary potassium supplementation vary greatly among individuals
justification: The authors explicitly state in the conclusion: 'the GenSalt replication study confirmed the large variations of BP responses to dietary sodium and potassium interventions and the CPT among individuals.' They also note the replication study 'provided further evidence to support several observations derived from the GenSalt study.'

original_authors: He, J.; Gu, D.; Chen, J.; Jaquish, C.; Rao, D.; Hixson, J.; Chen, J.; Duan, X.; Huang, J.; Chen, C.; Kelly, T.; Bazzano, L.; Whelton, P.
original_title: Gender difference in blood pressure responses to dietary sodium intervention in the GenSalt study
description: Blood pressure responses to the cold pressor test vary greatly among individuals
justification: The authors explicitly state in the conclusion: 'the GenSalt replication study confirmed the large variations of BP responses to dietary sodium and potassium interventions and the CPT among individuals.' They also note the replication study 'provided further evidence to support several observations derived from the GenSalt study.'

original_authors: Houben, K.; Havermans, R.; Wiers, R.
original_title: Learning to dislike alcohol: Conditioning negative implicit attitudes toward alcohol and its effect on drinking behavior
description: Evaluative conditioning with negative images reduces positive implicit evaluations of alcohol and decreases alcohol consumption among college students
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'the present preregistered study failed to replicate the results obtained by [Houben et al. 2010a]' and 'Overall, we found little evidence that a single session of EC was sufficient to change implicit evaluations of alcohol and drinking behaviors.' Bayesian analyses provided substantial support for the null hypotheses (BF01 = 5.71 and 5.01 for implicit evaluations and drinking behavior, respectively).

original_authors: Skurka, C.; Niederdeppe, J.; Romero-Canyas, R.; Acup, D.
original_title: Pathways of influence in emotional appeals: Benefits and tradeoffs of using fear or humor to promote climate change-related intentions and risk perceptions
description: Threat appeals about climate change increase perceived risk and activism intentions among young adults
justification: The authors explicitly state: "Unlike the original study, neither a threat appeal nor a humor appeal promoted young adults' intentions to engage in climate activism, nor did the threat appeal enhance climate risk perception." They note the failed fear induction likely explains the null results.

original_authors: Skurka, C.; Niederdeppe, J.; Romero-Canyas, R.; Acup, D.
original_title: Pathways of influence in emotional appeals: Benefits and tradeoffs of using fear or humor to promote climate change-related intentions and risk perceptions
description: Humor appeals about climate change increase activism intentions among young adults
justification: The authors state in the abstract "we fail to replicate these main effects" and in the discussion "neither a threat appeal nor a humor appeal promoted young adults' intentions to engage in climate activism." They note possible power issues but conclude the humor effect on intentions was not replicated.

original_authors: Skurka, C.; Niederdeppe, J.; Romero-Canyas, R.; Acup, D.
original_title: Pathways of influence in emotional appeals: Benefits and tradeoffs of using fear or humor to promote climate change-related intentions and risk perceptions
description: Age moderates the persuasive effect of humor appeals on climate change outcomes, with humor only persuading emerging adults (ages 18-25)
justification: The authors state: "We do replicate the finding that humor's persuasive influence is limited to the youngest young adults" and "we do, however, replicate age as a moderator of humor's effect on perceived risk, such that the humor appeal only persuaded emerging adults (ages 18-21.9)."

original_authors: Dvorak, A.; Hernandez-Ruiz, E.
original_title: Comparison of music stimuli to support mindfulness meditation
description: Four auditory stimuli of increasing complexity (Script, Beat, Harmony, and Melody) have different effects on mindfulness meditation, with less complex stimuli being more effective at supporting the mindfulness experience.
justification: This is a partial replication. The authors state: 'Different from the original study, we found that no auditory stimulus was significantly more effective in supporting the mindfulness experience' and conclude 'These partially replicated results indicate the need to explore alternative explanations.' The preference and usefulness rankings successfully replicated (Melody and Harmony ranked highest), but the main effectiveness outcome (MAAS scores) failed to show significant differences among conditions.

original_authors: Brady, W.; Wills, J.; Jost, J.; Tucker, J.; Van Bavel, J. J.
original_title: Emotion shapes the diffusion of moralized content in social networks
description: Emotional expressions related to morality (moral-emotional language) are associated with increased diffusion of political messages in online social networks
justification: The authors explicitly state: 'Our large, pre-registered replication and meta-analysis of 27 studies that included over 4,821,006 messages provides robust evidence of moral contagion in online social networks... These results provide strong evidence of the association between moral-emotional language and sharing and demonstrate the generalizability of moral contagion.' The mean effect size of the pre-registered replication (IRR = 1.17) closely matched the original study (IRR = 1.20).

original_authors: Johnson, R., Jr; Henkell, H.; Simon, E.; Zhu, J.
original_title: The self in conflict: the role of executive processes during truthful and deceptive responses about attitudes
description: Lying about attitudes produces enhanced medial frontal negativities (MFN), suppressed late positive components (LPC), and reduced pre-response positivities (PRP) in event-related potentials, indicating that deception relies on stronger cognitive control processes and response conflicts than being honest
justification: The authors explicitly conclude: "We could replicate the main ERP results of the study by [25]. Lying was accompanied by larger MFN, suppressed LPC and suppressed PRP amplitudes indicating that it was accompanied by more conflicts and was cognitively more challenging than truth telling." All main hypotheses were confirmed with decisive Bayes factors.

original_authors: Holbrook, C.; Izuma, K.; Deblieck, C.; Fessler, D.; Iacoboni, M.
original_title: Neuromodulation of group prejudice and religious belief
description: Downregulating posterior medial frontal cortex via transcranial magnetic stimulation reduces religious belief when participants are reminded of death
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "This pre-registered study replicated the prior finding that downregulating pMFC via cTBS reduces self-reported religious belief in the context of a recent, vivid reminder of death and bodily decomposition." The effect was statistically significant (p=0.038 for positive beliefs, p=0.024 for negative beliefs).

original_authors: Holbrook, C.; Izuma, K.; Deblieck, C.; Fessler, D.; Iacoboni, M.
original_title: Neuromodulation of group prejudice and religious belief
description: Downregulating posterior medial frontal cortex via transcranial magnetic stimulation reduces derogation of critical out-group members
justification: The authors explicitly state: "Departing from the findings of the prior study, we observed no effect of downregulating pMFC on group bias" (p=0.558). They note this may be due to using collegiate rather than national in-group framing, concluding "a putative effect of downregulating pMFC on group bias does not robustly generalize."

original_authors: Baca-García, E.; Diaz-Sastre, C.; De Leon, J.; Saiz-Ruiz, J.
original_title: The relationship between menstrual cycle phases and suicide attempts
description: Suicide attempts during menses are significantly more frequent than during other phases of the menstrual cycle in fertile women
justification: The abstract explicitly states 'this naturalistic study replicates a small but significant increase of suicide attempts during the menses.' The conclusion confirms: 'Our replication study verified this finding. Thus, both studies combined suggest that menses is associated with a significant increase of suicide attempts by a factor of 1.68.'

original_authors: Heintzelman, S.; Trent, J.; King, L.
original_title: Encounters with objective coherence and the experience of meaning in life
description: Exposure to coherent (versus incoherent) external stimuli increases self-reported meaning in life
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "The results of the present attempt failed to replicate the original findings of Heintzelman et al. [11] in that perceived MIL did not appear to statistically differ between the coherent and incoherent groups following exposure to their respective stimuli." Both Study 2 (tree photographs, p = 0.554, d = 0.06) and Study 4 (linguistic triads, p = 0.399, d = 0.099) showed null results, with Bayesian analyses providing moderate to strong evidence for the null hypothesis.

original_authors: Wadhwa, M.; Zhang, K.
original_title: This number just feels right: the impact of roundedness of price numbers on product evaluations
description: In emotional contexts, rounded prices increase purchase likelihood, while in cognitive contexts, non-rounded prices increase purchase likelihood, mediated by a sense of 'feeling right'
justification: The authors explicitly state: "Our results did not unambiguously support the rounded price effect and provide evidence against the proposed mediation." The critical interaction was not significant for either product tested (p = 0.436 for binoculars), and Bayes factors showed "strong evidence in favour of the null hypothesis" (BF r0 = 0.009).

original_authors: Proverbio, A.; Massetti, G.; Rizzi, E.; Zani, A.
original_title: Skilled musicians are not subject to the McGurk effect
description: Skilled musicians are not subject to the McGurk effect, an audiovisual speech perception illusion where conflicting visual and auditory cues lead to misperception of speech sounds
justification: The replication found the opposite of the original claim. The authors conclude: 'musicians are subject to the McGurk effect, and to at least as much extent (if not more) as non-musicians are.' The replication found musicians showed a statistically significant McGurk effect (p < 0.001) that was numerically and significantly larger than non-musicians', directly contradicting the original study's title claim.

original_authors: Young, L.; Saxe, S.
original_title: When ignorance is no excuse: different roles for intent across moral domains
description: Innocent intentions exculpate harm violations more than purity violations, reflecting a mental state × moral domain interaction effect
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "we successfully replicate the reduced exculpatory value of innocent intentions in purity (versus harm) violations." The replication Bayes factor was 4.7 × 10^8, indicating strong evidence for a consistent effect.

original_authors: Hamlin, J.; Wynn, K.; Bloom, P.
original_title: Social evaluation by preverbal infants
description: Preverbal infants display a preference for helpful over hindering characters when prompted to choose between them
justification: The authors explicitly state: "only 50% of infants did so in our study (16 of 32). Therefore, we could not reproduce the original findings." They further note that their proportion of 50% helper choices "falls outside the value range (0.59-1.0) defined by the 95% prediction interval" and "thus cannot be considered confirmatory."

original_authors: Smith S
original_title: A positive-negative mode of population covariation links brain connectivity, demographics and behavior
description: Canonical correlation analysis reveals a primary mode of covariation linking functional brain connectivity patterns with behavioral and demographic subject measures along a positive-negative axis, where positive qualities (higher income, education, cognitive performance) correlate positively with specific connectivity patterns, particularly in the default mode network, and negative qualities (substance use, rule-breaking) correlate negatively
justification: The authors met 2 of 3 pre-registered replication criteria: Mode 2 explained statistically significant variance in both connectomes and subject measures (criterion 1), and showed significant correlation between weights (criterion 3), but the magnitude of variance explained was smaller than predicted (criterion 2 failed). The authors state "our analysis shows that 9-to 10-year-old children exhibit the same basic phenomenon that was reported by Smith et al. in young adults" while acknowledging the primary mode was Mode 2 rather than Mode 1 and correlation was weaker (r=0.44 vs r=0.87).

original_authors: Johnson, M.; Higgins, J.; Norman, K.; Sederberg, P.; Smith, T.; Johnson, M.
original_title: Foraging for thought: an inhibition-of-return-like effect resulting from directing attention within working memory
description: Working memory representations that have just been refreshed are more slowly accessible immediately afterwards, showing an inhibition-of-return-like effect in working memory
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: 'The results of the present replication study replicate and confirm this inhibition-of-return-like effect in working memory' and 'the current replication study shows that the inhibition-of-return-like effect in working memory can reliably be observed across different laboratories and languages.' Strong Bayesian evidence (BF=28) supported the main hypothesis.

original_authors: Reiter, A.; Kanske, P.; Eppinger, B.; Li, S.
original_title: The aging of the social minddifferential effects on components of social understanding
description: Older adults show preserved empathy, enhanced compassion, but declined Theory of Mind (perspective-taking) compared to younger adults
justification: The authors explicitly state "we mainly succeeded in replicating the results" and "We were able to replicate the effect of age on empathy and compassion... Concerning ToM we replicated the effect of age on ToM accuracy." All primary effects were successfully replicated, with only a minor discrepancy in ToM reaction time.

original_authors: Newman, G.; Cain, D.
original_title: Tainted altruism: when doing some good is worse than doing no good at all
description: Observers view a person's choices as less ethical when that person has acted in response to both altruistic and selfish motivations, as compared with purely selfish interests
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: 'we readily reproduced the main results in the original studies quite closely' and describe it as 'a highly successful replication of Newman & Cain's second experiment' with results that 'closely resembled' the original findings across both experiments.

original_authors: Newman, G.; Cain, D.
original_title: Tainted altruism: when doing some good is worse than doing no good at all
description: The tainted altruism effect extends to behavioral intentions, with people willing to forgo the opportunity to earn more money for a charity if the person raising the money also earns a substantial profit
justification: The authors report 'a highly successful replication' with participants in the Charity condition rating Daniel as significantly less moral than in the Corporate condition (p = 0.004), and behavioral choice data showing 'the match between the original and replication functions underscores the broad success of the present replication.'

original_authors: Hickok, G.; Farahbod, H.; Saberi, K.
original_title: The rhythm of perception: entrainment to acoustic rhythms induces subsequent perceptual oscillation
description: Rhythmic auditory stimulation (amplitude-modulated noise) causes subsequent perceptual oscillation, such that target detection accuracy fluctuates based on the phase of the preceding rhythm
justification: The authors state in the Discussion: "In a large sample, we found robust evidence supporting that target detection accuracy is significantly influenced by the phase of preceding amplitude-modulated noise... Our findings replicate and extend those of Hickok et al. [20]." The statistical analysis confirmed sinusoidal oscillation (p = 0.001) with an extremely large Bayes factor (BF₁₀ = 3.235 × 10¹⁷).

original_authors: Mazor, M.; Moran, R.; Fleming, S.
original_title: Metacognitive asymmetries in visual perception
description: Brain regions show quadratic modulation of decision confidence that is specific to detection tasks (presence/absence decisions) compared to discrimination tasks (stimulus identity decisions), particularly in frontopolar cortex, temporoparietal junction, and superior temporal sulcus
justification: The authors successfully replicated the quadratic modulation of confidence in prefrontal and parietal cortices, but failed to replicate the key theoretical finding of detection-specificity. They explicitly state: 'The current pre-registered, hypothesis-driven replication provides an unbiased test of this effect, which resulted in a failure to replicate it.' However, they did replicate the basic quadratic effect, making this a partial replication.

original_authors: Will, P.; Merritt, E.; Jenkins, R.; Kingstone, A.
original_title: The Medusa effect reveals levels of mind perception in pictures
description: Pictures with lower abstraction levels (a picture of a person) are perceived to convey more mind (Realness, Agency, and Experience) than pictures with higher abstraction levels (a picture of a picture of a person).
justification: The authors explicitly state: "This present study successfully replicated the Medusa effect... These results supported our H1, as well as indicating successful replication of Will et al.'s [2] Experiment 2." All three dimensions (Realness, Agency, Experience) showed significantly higher ratings for L1 than L2 (all p < 0.001).

original_authors: Will, P.; Merritt, E.; Jenkins, R.; Kingstone, A.
original_title: The Medusa effect reveals levels of mind perception in pictures
description: Pictures with lower abstraction levels lead to higher prosocial behavior, with participants allocating more money to recipients depicted at lower abstraction levels (L1) than higher abstraction levels (L2) in a dictator game.
justification: The authors conclude: "Our H2 were fully supported, indicating the success of the replication of Will et al.'s [2] Experiment 5." Participants allocated significantly more money to L1 than L2 recipients (p = 0.01384), successfully replicating the behavioral effect of the Medusa phenomenon.

original_authors: Michotte, A.
original_title: The perception of causality
description: Visual impressions of causality occur when observing simple animations of moving geometrical objects, specifically the launching effect where one object is perceived as making another object move by bumping into it
justification: The authors report mixed results across 14 experiments testing various aspects of the launching effect. They state 'six hypotheses were supported by the results, six partly supported and six not supported' and note 'some significant divergences from results reported by Michotte' including effects of delay, fixation manipulations, and contextual factors that eliminated the effect even when typical stimulus features were present.

original_authors: Michotte, A.
original_title: The perception of causality
description: In the entraining effect, two objects move together after contact and the first moving object is perceived as pushing or carrying the other one
justification: The authors found partial support for the entraining effect across multiple experiments. The general discussion notes that 'entraining might be a more pervasive and stronger causal impression than launching under most circumstances,' but also reports significant divergences from Michotte's predictions, including 'lack of effect of relative speed manipulations on the entraining effect' and 'no evidence that the entraining effect occurs if the chased object continues at the same or slower speed after contact.'

original_authors: Baron, J.; Szymanska, E.
original_title: Heuristics and biases in charity
original_journal: The science of giving: experimental approaches to the study of charity (eds DM Oppenheimer, CY Olivola)
description: People exhibit non-utilitarian heuristics when donating to charity, including preferences for lower perceived waste/overhead, lower past costs, ingroup beneficiaries, diversification between charities, and voluntary over forced charity mechanisms
justification: The authors explicitly conclude: "at least four of our five hypotheses were found to replicate, we conclude this as being a successful replication." They found support for waste/overhead (d = 0.70), past costs (d = 0.59), ingroup preference (d = 0.52), and diversification (d = 0.63-1.18) effects, with mixed but nominally positive results for forced charity.

original_authors: Norton, M.; Frost, J.; Ariely, D.
original_title: Less is more: the lure of ambiguity, or why familiarity breeds contempt
description: People believe they will like someone more when they know more about them (lay intuition about knowledge and liking)
justification: The authors state in the Discussion: "We were able to replicate the original finding from Studies 1a and 1b that people expected they would like a target more when they knew more about them."

original_authors: Norton, M.; Frost, J.; Ariely, D.
original_title: Less is more: the lure of ambiguity, or why familiarity breeds contempt
description: More information about a person is associated with decreased liking (the 'less is more' effect)
justification: The authors explicitly state: "In our replication of Study 2, we failed to find support for a linear relationship between the number of traits presented and the degree of liking towards the target" and "our results challenge the less is more effect and suggest no significant impact of knowledge on liking."

original_authors: Fox, C.; Rottenstreich, Y.
original_title: Partition priming in judgment under uncertainty
description: Individuals' probability judgments under ignorance exhibit partition dependence, where the linguistic framing of a question (case vs. class partition) influences probability assessments even when the target event remains the same
justification: The authors explicitly concluded the replication as "(mostly) successful with effects generally weaker than the ones reported in the target article." They successfully replicated Studies 1a Items 1 and 2, Study 1b, and Study 3, but failed to find support for Study 1a Item 3 and Study 4. This mixed pattern represents a partial replication across multiple studies testing the same phenomenon in different contexts.

original_authors: Fox, C.; Rottenstreich, Y.
original_title: Partition priming in judgment under uncertainty
description: Partition dependence affects decision making under ignorance, where individuals' categorical choices (without numerical responses) show greater preference for risky options when those options have a higher partition-dependent ignorance prior
justification: For Study 4 specifically, the authors stated they "failed to find support" and found "no support for differences in the proportion of participants selecting the second option (uncertain high payment) between the case and the class condition" (z = 0.81, p = 0.415). The replication results "did not provide evidence for partition dependence in decision making."

original_authors: Nitsche, M.; Schauenburg, A.; Lang, N.; Liebetanz, D.; Exner, C.; Paulus, W.; Tergau, F.
original_title: Facilitation of Implicit Motor Learning by Weak Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation of the Primary Motor Cortex in the Human
description: Anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) over the primary motor cortex enhances implicit motor sequence learning in the serial reaction time task
justification: The authors explicitly state: 'Contrary to our expectations, we found no evidence that 1 mA anodal tDCS improves motor sequence learning.' The Bayes factor (0.153) provided 'substantial evidence against the hypothesis that tDCS can enhance motor sequence learning,' and they describe this as a 'non-replication of one of the presumably most reliable tDCS effects.'

original_authors: Felizardo K; Salleh N; Martins R; Mendes E; Macdonell S; Maldonado J
original_title: Using visual text mining to support the study selection activity in systematic literature reviews
original_journal: 5 th International Symposium on Empirical Software Engineering and Measurement (ESEM)
description: Visual text mining (VTM) techniques improve both the performance (speed) and effectiveness (correctness) of primary study selection in systematic literature reviews
justification: The replication confirmed one main finding (VTM speeds up study selection, p=0.010) but only partially replicated the effectiveness finding. The authors state that 'the use of VTM did not improve the effectiveness of the study selection activity in comparison to a manual reading approach' overall, though subsequent analysis revealed this effect is moderated by experience level: 'The effectiveness of the primary study selection activity carried out by PhDs using VTM is better than that achieved by reading the papers' but not for Master's students.

original_authors: Meltzoff, A.; Borton, R.
original_title: Intermodal matching by human neonates
description: One-month-old infants can transfer information about shape (smooth vs. nubby pacifiers) from oral touch to visual recognition, preferentially looking at matching visual stimuli
justification: The authors explicitly state: "The analyses of these three experiments provided no evidence that 1-month-olds can transfer information about the shape of smooth and nubby stimuli between touch and vision...even when we replicated exactly the methods described by [Meltzoff & Borton], we failed to find evidence for transfer."

original_authors: Harris, M.; Harris, R.; Bochner, S.
original_title: Fat, four-eyed, and female: Stereotypes of obesity, glasses and gender
description: Overweight targets are rated more negatively than average weight targets on personality and behavioral descriptors including active, attractive, athletic, hardworking, popular, and successful
justification: The authors concluded that the replication was successful, stating "there were no significant differences in effect sizes between the studies suggesting that there has been little change in obesity stereotypes over the past 30 years" and "There were a number of large effect sizes in the current study... given that there were no differences in effect size when compared with the Harris et al. study in 1982."

original_authors: Lackner, C.; Sabbagh, M.; Hallinan, E.; Liu, X.; Holden, J.
original_title: Dopamine receptor D4 gene variation predicts preschoolers' developing theory of mind
description: Children with two short alleles in DRD4 VNTR 48 bp (<6 repeats) outperform children with one or two long alleles (≥6 repeats) in false belief tasks, independent of executive function performance
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "We found no association between either of the sampled genetic markers (DRD4 VNTR 48 bp, COMT rs4680, OXTR rs53576) on Theory of Mind ability at the age of 50-70 months" and "our replication attempt of [19]...did not provide any evidence for associations between the three sampled genetic markers and Theory of Mind ability."

original_authors: Axelrod, V.; Rees, G.; Lavidor, M.; Bar, M.
original_title: Increasing propensity to mind-wander with transcranial direct current stimulation
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
description: Anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) applied to the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex increases the propensity to mind-wander during a sustained attention task
justification: The authors found strong evidence against the original effect, stating "there was extreme evidence (BF replication = 0.002) that the original study was not replicated" and concluded "there is no support for the supposition that bipolar anodal tDCS...can influence the propensity to mindwander. On the contrary, we found substantive evidence against the existence of such an effect."

original_authors: Hickok, G.; Farahbod, H.; Saberi, K.
original_title: The rhythm of perception: Entrainment to acoustic rhythms induces subsequent perceptual oscillation
description: Entrainment to amplitude-modulated acoustic rhythms (3 Hz) induces subsequent cyclic perceptual oscillations in the detection of auditory tone targets
justification: The authors conclude: "Neither of our experiments showed a significant entrainment effect at the group level... The current study does not demonstrate a consistent impact of a preceding rhythmically modulated background noise on the detection of upcoming near-threshold tone targets... Our findings raise questions about the robustness of the paradigm used in the original study."

original_authors: Knox, J.E.; Mogan, J.
original_title: Characteristics of 'best' and 'worst' clinical teachers as perceived by university nursing faculty and students
description: Best clinical teachers are good role models who enjoy nursing and teaching, demonstrate clinical skills and judgment, and encourage mutual respect; worst clinical teachers are not good role models
justification: The authors explicitly state in the conclusion: 'The replication study reflected similar faculty and student perceptions to those found by Knox & Mogan (1987). Such similar findings confirm the tool's reliability over time and with different samples.' Both studies found that being a good role model and encouraging mutual respect were the most distinguishing characteristics between best and worst clinical teachers.

original_authors: Phillips, E.
original_title: The effects of language anxiety on students' oral test performance and attitudes
description: Higher levels of foreign language anxiety are associated with poorer performance on oral examinations in university foreign language students
justification: The authors explicitly state: "Overall, our study fulfilled the aims of replication, which were the reliability and the generalizability of Phillips's outcomes" and "Not only do our results support Phillips's findings, but also they lend weight to the body of anxiety literature." The core finding of a moderate negative correlation between anxiety and oral performance was replicated successfully.

original_authors: Christensen P; Gram L; Kragh-Ssrensen P; Nielsen S
original_title: Afternoon cortisol levels before (spontaneous) and after suppression with dexamethasone or oxazepam in depressed patients
description: Afternoon plasma cortisol levels (spontaneous and after suppression with dexamethasone or oxazepam) correlate with age, type of depression, severity of depression, and stress/distress symptoms in depressed patients
justification: The present study failed to demonstrate significant correlations between cortisol levels and age or quality of depression, which were found in the earlier study. However, the consistent finding across all studies was the high correlation with stress/distress items (HRSD items 8+9+10+12), suggesting partial replication with some key findings not reproduced.

original_authors: Fowers, B.; Olson, D.
original_title: Predicting marital success with PREPARE: A predictive validity study
original_journal: Journal of Marital and Family Therapy
description: PREPARE premarital inventory scores predict subsequent marital status (happy marriage vs. divorce/separation) with approximately 80% accuracy in a 3-year follow-up study
justification: The authors explicitly state in their discussion: 'The purpose of this study was to replicate a previous study regarding the predictive validity of PREPARE. In general, the findings were very compatible, providing greater confidence in that predictive capacity than could be justified by a single study.' The abstract confirms: 'This study clearly replicated the previous findings which demonstrated the predictive validity of PREPARE... PREPARE predicted, with about 80% accuracy, couples who got divorced from those that were happily married.'

original_authors: Tang, H.; Ng, J.
original_title: Googling for a diagnosis-use of Google as a diagnostic aid: internet based study
description: Using Google searches with keywords from complex case reports can assist clinicians in reaching correct diagnoses
justification: The replication found that Google-aided diagnosis succeeded in 42% of veterinary cases (95% CI 29%-55%), which does not differ statistically from the original 58% rate in human medicine (P = .18). The authors conclude that 'searching Google appears to retrieve relevant veterinary resources that assisted a generalist veterinarian in correctly diagnosing' challenging cases, successfully demonstrating the effect in a veterinary context.

original_authors: Kreibig, S.; Samson, A.; Gross, J.
original_title: The psychophysiology of mixed emotional states
description: Physiological responses to amusement, disgust, and a mixed emotional state (amusing-disgusting) show distinct patterns, with the mixed emotional state differing in both intensity and pattern from both pure constituent emotions
justification: The authors state that "Three levels of analysis produced converging evidence for replicability" and that "Primary analyses produced similar findings to our previous study, demonstrating (a) univariate differentiation of the mixed emotional state from its pure constituent emotions on physiological response variables, and (b) intensity and pattern differences of the multivariate physiological response profile of the mixed emotional state from those of pure amusement and pure disgust."

original_authors: Hewig, J.; Kretschmer, N.; Trippe, R.; Hecht, H.; Coles, M.; Holroyd, C.; Miltner, W.
original_title: Why humans deviate from rational choice
description: Negative affect, larger skin conductance response (SCR), and larger feedback-related negativity (FRN) amplitudes predict rejection of unfair monetary offers in ultimatum and dictator games, demonstrating non-rational decision-making behavior.
justification: The authors explicitly state 'only half of the six targets were successfully replicated.' While behavioral patterns and subjective ratings matched the original study, psychophysiological effects differed substantially: SCR effects were absent, FRN showed a quadratic rather than linear pattern, and the regression model failed to explain expected variance. The authors conclude they 'could conceptually replicate the finding that human behavior is not rational, yet unfolds in a somewhat different [way] from what [the original study] had originally proposed.'

original_authors: Nearey, T.; Hillenbrand, J.
original_title: Some effects of duration on vowel recognition - Experiment 1
original_journal: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
description: Altering vowel duration has a modest effect on vowel recognition, with vowels of long typical duration shifting to shorter-duration neighbors when shortened, and vice versa
justification: The authors state: 'There were many features in common between the findings of experiments 1 and 2. In both experiments, the effect of altering vowel duration was seen to be relatively modest overall... Further, the duration-related effects that were observed in both experiments were quite sensible.' Both experiments replicated the same qualitative patterns of duration effects on vowel identity.

original_authors: Toi, P.; Jang, H.K.; Min, K.; Kim, S.G.; Lee, S.K.; Lee, J.H.; Kwag, J.; Park, J.Y.
original_title: In vivo direct imaging of neuronal activity at high temporospatial resolution
description: Direct imaging of neuronal activity (DIANA) by fMRI can detect neuronal activity-related signals with high temporal resolution (peak at ~12 ms in thalamus and ~25 ms in primary somatosensory cortex) following whisker stimulation in anesthetized mice at 9.4T
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: 'we could not replicate the original DIANA findings even with more extensive averaging, a more precise and steady anesthetic protocol, and higher field strength when no improper data selection was performed.' They found no direct neuronal-related signal in extensively averaged fMRI studies (up to 1050 trials) and conclude that 'the original DIANA findings are likely to be artifacts due to unreported data processing approaches of noisy data with limited temporal points and trials.'

original_authors: Lombardi, V.; Ruscetti, F.W.; Das Gupta, J.; Pfost, M.A.; Hagen, K.S.; Peterson, D.L.; Ruscetti, S.K.; Bagni, R.K.; Petrow-Sadowski, C.; Gold, B.; Dean, M.; Silverman, R.H.; Mikovits, J.A.
original_title: Detection of an infectious retrovirus, XMRV, in blood cells of patients with chronic fatigue syndrome
description: XMRV (xenotropic murine leukemia virus-related virus) is present in blood cells of patients with chronic fatigue syndrome
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: "Given the lack of evidence for XMRV or XMRV-like viruses in our cohort of CFS patients, as well as the lack of these viruses in a set of patients that previously tested positive, we feel that that XMRV is not associated with CFS." They found no XMRV in any samples using multiple detection methods.

original_authors: Yang, X.; Lo, D.
original_title: TLEL: A Two-layer Ensemble Learning Approach for Just-in-time Defect Prediction
description: A two-layer ensemble learning approach (TLEL) combining decision trees with bagging to build random forests can achieve statistically significantly better performance in just-in-time defect prediction compared to previously tested learning algorithms
justification: The authors explicitly state that 'Our results from the replicated experiment are consistent with the original' and report that 'The F1 scores of the layers of the original and replicated TLEL are statistically equivalent between the original and replicated experiments.' All main findings were successfully reproduced across all six datasets.

original_authors: Stoyanov D; Kandilarova S; Borgwardt S; Stieglitz R; Hugdahl K; Kostianev S
original_title: On Translational Cross-Validation of Clinical Self-Evaluation Scale and fMRI
description: Patients with major depressive disorder show increased neuronal activity in brain structures including the right supramarginal gyrus when processing diagnostically specific statements from the von Zerssen questionnaire compared to diagnostically neutral statements
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: "the results obtained in the current replication study allow us to confirm the main findings of the study we replicated" and note "overlapping results in the area of the right supramarginal gyrus in both the previous and replication studies."

original_authors: Schlemm, E.; Frey, B.; Mayer, C.; Petersen, M.; Fiehler, J.; Hanning, U.; Kühn, S.; Twerenbold, R.; Gallinat, J.; Gerloff, C.; Thomalla, G.; Cheng, B.
original_title: Equalization of brain state occupancy accompanies cognitive impairment in cerebral small vessel disease
description: Greater white matter hyperintensity volume from cerebral small vessel disease is associated with reduced time spent in high-occupancy brain states characterized by default mode network activation/suppression, which in turn is associated with executive dysfunction and reduced processing speed
justification: The authors explicitly state: "In this pre-registered cross-sectional study, we replicated the key findings of [39] in an independent population-based sample" and "we confirmed that the severity of cerebral small vessel disease is associated with the time spent in high-occupancy brain states" with statistically significant results (P = 5.01×10⁻⁸ for primary hypothesis, P = 0.0116 for secondary hypothesis).

original_authors: Motto, J. A.
original_title: Newspaper strikes and suicide rates in Detroit
description: Complete cessation of newspaper publication during strikes reduces suicide rates, especially among women under age 35
justification: The authors state they "did not find any relationship between the suicide rate and the partial cessation of newspaper publication" overall, and their findings "contrast with his study of complete cessation of newspaper publication in Detroit." However, consistent with Motto's Detroit findings, they observed that "for women in the younger age groups, 15-24 years and 25-34 years, the suicide rates during the strike period were the lowest in the six years studied" - a partial replication of the subgroup effect.

original_authors: Collisson, B.; Howell, J.; Harig, T.
original_title: Foodie calls: When women date men for a free meal (rather than a relationship)
description: Dark Triad personality traits (narcissism, Machiavellianism, psychopathy) and traditional gender role beliefs predict women's engagement in foodie calls and the perceived acceptability of this behavior
justification: The authors state "our study revealed mixed results" and describe "partially replicated findings." The pooled sample found gender role beliefs as the strongest predictor, but the general Dark Triad factor was not significant. Results varied by country: Poland successfully replicated, UK partially replicated, and the US sample showed that Dark Triad general factor failed to predict foodie calls or acceptability.

original_authors: Fischer, P.; Postmes, T.; Koeppl, J.; Conway, L.; Fredriksson, T.
original_title: The meaning of collective terrorist threat: Understanding the subjective causes of terrorism reduces its negative psychological impact
description: Understanding terrorists' motives reduces the negative psychological impact of terrorism, specifically reducing perceived threat and improving emotional well-being
justification: The authors state they "partly replicated" the findings: "For emotional well-being... we partially replicated the results from the original experiments" but "For perceived threat... we did not replicate the findings of the original experiment." The conclusion states "the reanalysis of the effect sizes across all experiments does not show convincing evidence for the hypothesis."

original_authors: Hung, S.; Styles, S.; Hsieh, P.
original_title: Can a word sound like a shape before you have seen it? Sound-shape mapping prior to conscious awareness
description: Congruent sound-shape combinations (e.g., kiki in an angular shape, bubu in a round shape) break through continuous flash suppression faster than incongruent combinations, demonstrating that sound-shape mapping occurs before conscious awareness
justification: The authors state in their Discussion: "we obtained converging evidence for the notion that congruent sound-shape stimuli gain preferential access to awareness. We believe this provides a solid basis to now explore the boundary conditions of the effect." Although the effect size was smaller than the original (Cohen's d = 0.21 vs 0.42), the replication successfully demonstrated the same phenomenon with strong statistical support (BF10 = 6.38, p = .003).

original_authors: Zajonc, R.; Heingartner, A.; Herman, E.
original_title: Social enhancement and impairment of performance in the cockroach
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
description: The presence of an audience interacts with task difficulty to produce social facilitation (faster performance) in simple tasks and social inhibition (slower performance) in complex tasks
justification: The authors state that their "analyses revealed evidence clearly speaking against the proposed interaction" and that while they replicated social inhibition in complex tasks, they "found no social facilitation in the simple task but robust evidence for very opposite." The critical Audience × Task Difficulty interaction showed no effect (F = 0.02, p = .882).

original_authors: Shalvi, S.; Eldar, O.; Bereby-Meyer, Y.
original_title: Honesty requires time (and lack of justifications)
description: Time pressure increases dishonest reporting in a die-roll task where participants have financial incentive to inflate their reported outcome
justification: Both preregistered direct replications found no evidence that time pressure increases cheating. The authors conclude: 'our findings indicate that the original study by [15] may have overestimated the true effect of time pressure on cheating or the generality of the effect beyond the original context.' PDR 2 reached decisive evidence for the null hypothesis (BF01 = 10.14).

original_authors: Farooqui, A.; Manly, T.
original_title: Anticipatory control through associative learning of subliminal relations: Invisible may be better than visible
description: Subliminal cues can reduce task-switching costs more effectively than supraliminal cues, demonstrating that invisible cues are better than visible ones for modulating cognitive control
justification: The authors explicitly state "We failed to replicate the results found by [14], which suggested that participants were more effective at modulating switch costs following subliminal cues." With double the original sample size, they found no evidence that subliminal cues reduced switch costs, and equivalence tests in Experiment 2 confirmed the effect was statistically equivalent to zero.

original_authors: Kupor, D. M.; Laurin, K.; Levav, J.
original_title: Anticipating divine protection? Reminders of God can increase nonmoral risk taking
description: Religious primes (thinking about God) increase nonmoral risk-taking among believers through a mechanism of anticipating divine protection
justification: The authors explicitly state: "We could not replicate either study by any of four replication metrics... the totality of evidence speaks against the possibility that religious primes increase nonmoral risk taking... It may be worth treating the anticipating-divine-protection hypothesis with skepticism."

original_authors: Miller, S.; Maner, J.
original_title: Sick body, vigilant mind: The biological immune system activates the behavioral immune system
description: Participants who had recently been ill show heightened attentional bias toward disfigured faces compared to participants who had not recently been ill
justification: The authors explicitly state: "Yet given the results from this direct replication, it should not be taken as evidence for such a relation." The critical interaction between illness recency and face type was not significant (p = .173), and the equivalence test showed the effect size was significantly smaller than what the original study could detect.

original_authors: Mueller, P.; Oppenheimer, D.
original_title: The pen is mightier than the keyboard: Advantages of longhand over laptop note taking
description: Longhand note-taking improves conceptual understanding of lecture material compared to laptop note-taking, due to better encoding of information
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: "results did not support the idea that longhand note taking improves performance via better encoding of information." Contrary to the original findings, the replication found no significant difference in conceptual-application performance between laptop and longhand conditions (Hedges's g = -0.13, 95% CI = [-0.45, 0.20]).

original_authors: Toner, K.; Leary, M.; Asher, M.; Jongman-Sereno, K.
original_title: Feeling superior is a bipartisan issue: Extremity (not direction) of political views predicts perceived belief superiority
description: Political extremity (not direction) predicts perceived belief superiority, such that both extreme liberals and extreme conservatives report higher belief superiority than moderates
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "We successfully replicated the finding that individuals with more extreme attitudes, both liberal and conservative, reported higher belief superiority. Therefore, these patterns appear to be robust across samples, time, and measures."

original_authors: Toner, K.; Leary, M.; Asher, M.; Jongman-Sereno, K.
original_title: Feeling superior is a bipartisan issue: Extremity (not direction) of political views predicts perceived belief superiority
description: Conservatives have higher dogmatism scores than liberals
justification: The replication confirmed the original linear effect (conservatives higher dogmatism) but also found an additional curvilinear effect not reported in the original. The Discussion notes: "We successfully replicated this relationship" but also "Our research also revealed an important difference from prior work. Specifically, we found that individuals with more conservative or more liberal ideologies had higher dogmatism scores."

original_authors: Pennycook, G.; Mcphetres, J.; Zhang, Y.; Lu, J.; Rand, D.
original_title: Fighting COVID-19 misinformation on social media: Experimental evidence for a scalable accuracynudge intervention
description: Asking people to think about the accuracy of a single headline improves truth discernment in subsequent sharing intentions for COVID-19 news headlines on social media
justification: The first stage of replication (n=701) failed completely (p=.67). The pooled second stage (N=1,583) found a significant but substantially attenuated effect—treatment effect was 1.4 times higher versus 2.8 times in the original, representing 50% attenuation. The authors state "the effect size of the accuracy-nudge intervention appears small, and we advise scholars that variation can be expected across replications" and note the effect disappeared for attentive participants.

original_authors: Guo, L.; Trueblood, J.; Diederich, A.
original_title: Thinking fast increases framing effects in risky decision making
description: Time pressure increases the magnitude of the framing effect in risky decision-making, where people show greater risk aversion for gains and risk seeking for losses when decision time is limited
justification: The authors explicitly state: 'First, we verified that we replicated [Guo et al. 2017] results by conducting a 2 (frame: gain, loss) × 2 (time constraint: none, 1 s) repeated measures ANOVA... the framing effect was larger when participants had limited time...than when they had unlimited time... Thus, our results replicate those of prior studies.'

original_authors: Cook, J.; Lewandowsky, S.; Ecker, U.
original_title: Neutralizing misinformation through inoculation: Exposing misleading argumentation techniques reduces their influence
description: Misinformation about climate change (using fake experts) reduces acceptance of anthropogenic global warming, and inoculation messages preceding misinformation neutralize this negative effect
justification: The authors explicitly state: 'we could not replicate the findings of [Cook et al.]; At least in our setting, the misinformation message and also inoculation preceding misinformation had hardly any effect on the climate-related attitudes under study.' The interventions showed no significant effects in the German sample.

original_authors: Nicolaou, N.; Patel, P.; Wolfe, M.
original_title: Testosterone and tendency to engage in self-employment
description: Left-hand 2D:4D digit ratio (a proxy for prenatal testosterone exposure) is negatively associated with self-employment, with lower 2D:4D indicating higher testosterone exposure and greater likelihood of being self-employed
justification: The authors explicitly state 'We thus fail to replicate their findings in the sense of finding a statistically significant (or suggestive) effect in the same direction' and conclude 'we find no substantive evidence of an association between 2D:4D and self-employment, contradicting the conclusions for left-hand 2D:4D in Nicolaou et al. (2018).'

original_authors: Archer, D.; Gartner, R.
original_title: Violent acts and violent times: A comparative approach to postwar homicide
description: Wars increase postwar homicide rates because they legitimize the use of violence as a means of conflict resolution
justification: The authors state they "were able to replicate their findings" using original methods, but note "when we applied multiple regression adjusting for potential confounders, the results became less consistent across wars... and over time." The time series results provided only "modest support," with stronger effects for WWI than WWII, and the extension to modern wars found "no support for the legitimation of violence argument."

original_authors: Somersan, S.
original_title: Death symbolism in matrilineal societies
description: Matrilineal societies exhibit a distinct pattern of death symbolism characterized by beliefs in ancestral spirits, reincarnation, and an afterlife whose quality is unconditional on earthly behavior
justification: The authors explicitly state in the abstract "None of her findings were supported in this replication study" and in the conclusion "I have identified sampling error as the most likely reason why I failed to replicate Somersan's (1984) tests of death symbolism." Three of four statistical tests that were significant in the original study were non-significant in the replication.

original_authors: Sumia, M.; Lindberg, N.; Työläjärvi, M.; Kaltiala-Heino, R.
original_title: Current and recalled childhood gender identity in community youth in comparison to referred adolescents seeking sex reassignment
description: Potentially clinically significant gender dysphoria can be measured in adolescent populations using the GIDYQ-A questionnaire, with prevalence rates of 2.2% in males and 0.5% in females among Finnish junior high school students
justification: The replication successfully used the same methodology (GIDYQ-A questionnaire in Finnish junior high schools) and confirmed measurable prevalence of gender dysphoria. The authors state: 'GD appears more common than it was 5 years earlier among Finnish junior high school students' and 'feelings of GD have increased in the adolescent population in Finland,' confirming both the measurement approach and detecting temporal changes.

original_authors: Haselton, M.
original_title: The sexual overperception bias: Evidence of a systematic bias in men from a survey of naturally occuring events
description: Women report being subject to opposite-sex sexual overperception far more often than underperception, while this difference is small for men, reflecting a systematic sexual overperception bias in men predicted by Error Management Theory
justification: The authors explicitly state: "All three original EMT generated hypotheses were strongly supported" and "The general pattern of findings suggests that this study of Norwegian students—using identical methodology—closely replicates Haselton's (2003) original findings of sex biases in sexual misperception of naturally occurring events."

original_authors: Ries, D.
original_title: Caregivers and the ministry of Alzheimer's disease. The American Journal of Alzheimer's Care and Related Disorders and Research
original_journal: The American Journal of Alzheimer's Care and Related Disorders and Research
description: Montana clergy demonstrate knowledge about Alzheimer's disease, and caregiving families hold varied expectations for and satisfaction with clergy support
justification: The replication showed mixed results. Clergy knowledge scores replicated successfully (p = 0.908), but the authors conclude that "responses of Kentuckiana families indicated less satisfaction with clergy support received than was the case in the Ries study," with significant differences in dissatisfaction with clergy understanding of the afflicted's needs (p = 0.019). The authors attribute differences to urban versus rural contexts rather than outright replication failure.

original_authors: Schooler, J.; Engstler-Schooler, T.
original_title: Verbal overshadowing of visual memories: Some things are better left unsaid
description: Verbally describing a person's appearance impairs later recognition memory for that person, with participants who described a robber being approximately 25% worse at identifying the robber in a lineup compared to a control condition
justification: The authors explicitly conclude that 'these findings reveal a robust verbal overshadowing effect' and that the studies 'provide clear evidence for verbal overshadowing.' RRR2, which matched the original task order, produced a meta-analytic effect size of -16.31% that was close to the original -25%, while RRR1 showed a smaller but still significant effect of -4.01%. The authors frame both as successful replications, with task order moderating effect size.

original_authors: Hart, W.; Albarracín, D.
original_title: Learning about what others were doing: Verb aspect and attributions of mundane and criminal intent for past actions
description: Actions described using imperfective grammatical aspect (e.g., 'was shooting') are judged as more intentional than actions described using perfective aspect (e.g., 'shot'), and are processed in greater detail
justification: The authors explicitly state: 'The results of this large-scale, multilab direct replication...are not consistent with the original result that actions described in imperfective aspect are considered to be more intentional.' The meta-analysis found d = -0.24 for criminal intentionality (95% CI: -0.50 to 0.02) and d = -0.08 for detailed processing (95% CI: -0.23 to 0.07), both close to zero and including zero in confidence intervals, compared to the original study's d = 0.67-0.77.

original_authors: Finkel, E.; Rusbult, C.; Kumashiro, M.; Hannon, P.
original_title: Dealing with betrayal in close relationships: Does commitment promote forgiveness?
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
description: Priming participants to think about their commitment to their romantic partner (vs. independence from their partner) causes reduced destructive forgiveness responses (exit and neglect) to hypothetical relationship betrayals
justification: The authors explicitly state "The results of this large-scale, multilab direct replication... are not consistent with the original result" and "we failed to replicate the pattern of findings." The manipulation check showed no effect on commitment (original: 1.33 points, RRR: .02 points), and there were no effects on exit (RRR: -.06, 95% CI: -.17 to .05) or neglect (RRR: -.06, 95% CI: -.18 to .07) forgiveness responses.

original_authors: Dijksterhuis, A.; Van Knippenberg, A.
original_title: The relation between perception and behavior, or how to win a game of Trivial Pursuit
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
description: Priming participants with a category associated with intelligence (professor) increases performance on a trivia test compared to priming with a category associated with lack of intelligence (soccer hooligans)
justification: The authors explicitly state in their General Discussion that 'the meta-analytic results of this multilab replication provided little empirical support for a difference in trivia performance' and that 'these experiments did not find the difference in trivia performance originally observed in Dijksterhuis and van Knippenberg's (1998) Experiment 4.' The meta-analytic effect was 0.14% (95% CI = [-0.71%, 1.00%]), essentially zero.

original_authors: Roberts, B.; Smith, J.; Jackson, J.; Edmonds, G.
original_title: Compensatory conscientiousness and health in older couples
description: Partner conscientiousness predicts better self-rated health and fewer physical limitations in older married couples, with a synergistic interaction effect where husbands high in both conscientiousness and neuroticism predict better health in their wives
justification: The authors conclude: "In this direct replication of [16], we found very similar results" and note that "ten out of fourteen of the originally statistically significant effects were statistically significant in this replication study." The focal effects of partner conscientiousness and the interaction between husbands' conscientiousness and neuroticism were successfully replicated.

original_authors: Srull, T.; Wyer, R.
original_title: The role of category accessibility in the interpretation of information about persons: Some determinants and implications
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
description: Exposing participants to hostility-related stimuli causes them to subsequently interpret ambiguous behaviors as more hostile
justification: The authors conclude: "Our results suggest that the procedures we used in this replication study are unlikely to produce an assimilative priming effect that researchers could practically and routinely detect." The meta-analytic effects were close to zero (0.08 points for protagonist ratings, -0.08 for behavior ratings) compared to the original ~3 scale point differences, with one measure going in the opposite direction.

original_authors: Mazar, N.; Amir, O.; Ariely, D.
original_title: The dishonesty of honest people: A theory of self-concept maintenance
description: Recalling the Ten Commandments (a moral reminder) reduces cheating on a problem-solving task compared to recalling neutral information
justification: The authors explicitly conclude: "In sum, we did not observe the predicted reduction in cheating following priming with the Ten Commandments. These results call into question the effectiveness of using the Ten Commandments as a moral prime to reduce cheating." The replication found an effect of d = -0.04 (95% CI = [-0.12, 0.04]), essentially zero and numerically opposite to the original effect of d = 0.48.

original_authors: Brookhart, M.; Freburger, J.; Ellis, K.; Wang, L.; Winkelmayer, W.; Kshirsagar, A.
original_title: Infection risk with bolus versus maintenance iron supplementation in hemodialysis patients
description: Hemodialysis patients receiving bolus iron dosing (frequent large doses) versus maintenance dosing have higher risks of infection-related hospitalization and death, with greatest risks in patients with dialysis catheters, but no association with cardiovascular outcomes
justification: The authors explicitly state that their findings were "remarkably similar" to the original study and that they are "Consistent with previous work". The hazard ratios for infection outcomes were nearly identical (1.08-1.17 in replication vs 1.05-1.11 in original), and both studies found no association with cardiovascular outcomes.

original_authors: Schindl, M.; Wassipaul, S.; Wagner, T.; Gstaltner, K.; Bethge, M.
original_title: Impact of functional capacity evaluation on patient-reported functional ability: an exploratory diagnostic before-after study
description: Performance of functional capacity evaluation (FCE) increases patient-reported functional ability as measured by the Spinal Function Sort (SFS) in patients with musculoskeletal trauma
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: "a significant increase in patient-reported functional ability after FCE was found in patients with musculoskeletal trauma in the original study, and the results were reproduced in two subsequent cohorts." The improvement was consistent across all cohorts (14.8, 14.8, and 15.2 points respectively) with overlapping 95% confidence intervals.

original_authors: Flaxman, A.; Joseph, J.; Murray, C.; Riley, I.; Lopez, A.
original_title: Performance of InSilicoVA for assigning causes of death to verbal autopsies: multisite validation study using clinical diagnostic gold standards
description: The InSilicoVA algorithm accurately assigns causes of death from verbal autopsy data, achieving specific performance metrics when validated against clinical diagnostic gold standards
justification: The authors explicitly state in the abstract "We failed to reproduce the results published in Flaxman et al." and in the Discussion section "Using publicly available data, we attempted and failed to replicate the evaluation study in Flaxman et al. [1]."

original_authors: Najar, H.; Joas, E.; Pålsson, E.; Landén, M.
original_title: Time effect on cardiometabolic risk indicators in patients with bipolar disorder: a longitudinal case-control study
description: Individuals with bipolar disorders show higher levels of cardiometabolic risk indicators (waist-to-hip ratio, BMI, blood pressure, atherogenic lipid profile) compared to general population controls, with worsening central obesity and blood pressure over time
justification: The authors state they "replicated the deterioration of WHR, SBP, and DBP in the patient group relative to the control group" and confirm that "findings regarding blood pressure were replicated." However, they also note they "did not replicate statistically significant baseline differences in WHR, TAG, TAG/HDL ratio, TChol/HDL-C ratio, and non-HDL-C between the two groups." This constitutes a partial replication where some key findings were confirmed while others were not.

original_authors: Potthast, N.; Neuner, F.; Catani, C.
original_title: When abuse primes addiction-automatic activation of alcohol concepts by child maltreatment related cues in emotionally abused alcoholics
description: Child maltreatment related cues automatically activate an associative memory network comprising alcohol-related responses in alcohol-dependent subjects with emotional abuse experiences
justification: The authors explicitly state: "Contrary to our hypothesis, we did not find a specific priming effect" and "this pattern of results could not be replicated in qualified detoxification setting." All statistical analyses showed no significant effects with effect sizes ranging from 0.00 to 0.02.

original_authors: Pechey, R.; Couturier, D.; Hollands, G.; Mantzari, E.; Munafò, M.; Marteau, T.
original_title: Does wine glass size influence sales for on-site consumption? A multiple treatment reversal design
description: Serving wine in larger glasses (370ml vs 300ml) increases wine sales by approximately 9.4% without changing portion sizes
justification: The authors explicitly state 'Overall, the results of the current study provide only a partial replication of previous findings.' While one comparison (510ml vs 370ml in Bar 1) showed a significant 10.5% increase, the key original comparison (370ml vs 300ml) failed to replicate in Bar 1, and Bar 2 showed no significant effects at all.

original_authors: Meen, E.; Blakley, B.; Quddusi, T.
original_title: Does intracochlear brain-derived nerve growth factor improve auditory brainstem click thresholds in sensorineural hearing loss?
description: A single intracochlear injection of BDNF improves auditory brainstem response (ABR) thresholds in guinea pigs with cisplatin-induced sensorineural hearing loss
justification: The authors explicitly state in the abstract: "Our original finding that Intracochlear BDNF can improve hearing in guinea pigs was confirmed" and in the discussion: "our results indicate that intracochlear BDNF is associated with lower thresholds of about 11 dB. The results of this study are consistent with some of our previous work."

original_authors: Tseng, P.; Bridgeman, B.
original_title: Improved change detection with nearby hands
description: Hand proximity to a visual display improves change detection sensitivity when colored squares briefly change color
justification: The authors explicitly state that Experiment 3 'attempted to replicate the near-hands advantage in a change detection paradigm' but 'was unable to do so', and Experiment 4 was 'a direct replication of Tseng and Bridgeman' in which 'still, no near-hands advantage was observed.' The conclusion emphasizes that 'the near-hands advantage may be very sensitive to small differences in procedure' and their null results suggest hand proximity effects are 'fragile.'

original_authors: Jalal, B.; Krishnakumar, D.; Ramachandran, V.
original_title: I feel contaminated in my fake hand": Obsessive-compulsive-disorder like disgust sensations arise from dummy during rubber hand illusion
description: Placing contamination-related stimuli on a rubber hand during the rubber hand illusion induces OCD-like disgust sensations when the rubber hand and participant's real hand are stroked synchronously
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: "the present study successfully replicated the main findings of Jalal et al." and "The results of the present study demonstrated that placing disgust-related stimuli on a rubber hand did in fact induce stronger OCD-like disgust reactions during the RHI as compared to the control condition."

original_authors: Wiles, D.; Kolakowska, T.; McNeil, M.; Mandelbrote, B. M.; Gelder, M. G.
original_title: Clinical significance of plasma chlorpromazine levels. I. Plasma levels of the drug, some of its metabolites and prolactin during acute treatment
description: Plasma chlorpromazine levels vary widely among patients and correlate poorly with dose; increased plasma prolactin is associated with higher plasma chlorpromazine levels and extrapyramidal symptoms; but these variables do not differ between patients with good versus poor treatment outcomes
justification: The authors state 'We confirmed our previous findings with two exceptions.' Multiple findings were successfully replicated (wide variability in plasma drug levels, correlation between prolactin and drug levels, association with extrapyramidal symptoms), but two specific findings failed to replicate (association between EPS and higher plasma CPZ levels, and the CPZ-sulphoxide/CPZ ratio difference between improved and non-improved patients). This represents a partial replication.

original_authors: Bryan, C.; Adams, G.; Monin, B.
original_title: When cheating would make you a cheater: implicating the self prevents unethical behavior
description: Noun-based self-identity language ('Don't be a cheater') prevents unethical behavior more effectively than verb-based language ('Don't cheat')
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: 'this study successfully replicated the results of Experiment 3 of Bryan et al. (2013) as a registered report without any deviation from the protocol... The results of our study supported the hypothesis that self-identity-related nouns of moral reminder curbed unethical behaviors more effectively.'

original_authors: Yu, R.; Mobbs, D.; Seymour, B.; Rowe, J.B.; Calder, A.J.
original_title: The neural signature of escalating frustration in humans
description: Goal proximity and expended effort independently increase participants' motivation during reward pursuit, and increase response force and self-reported frustration when blocked from obtaining a reward
justification: The authors state "we were able to replicate the effects of proximity and effort on arrow RTs and self-reported motivation and frustration" but also note "we were unable to replicate all the behavioral findings of Yu et al. (2014)" including differences in surprise ratings and confirm RT effects that emerged in their study but not the original, plus their force measurement failed due to technical issues.

original_authors: Schirmer, B.
original_title: Using verbal protocols to identify reading strategies of students who are deaf
original_journal: Journal of Deaf Studies and Deaf Education
description: Verbal protocol analysis (think-aloud methodology) can be used to examine the reading strategies of deaf students, and deaf readers use reading strategies similar to those of hearing readers in constructing meaning, monitoring comprehension, and evaluating comprehension.
justification: The authors explicitly state: 'This was the same finding as in the first study, so the replication study provides support for the reliability of this finding' and 'the consistency in the reading strategies used by the participants in both studies indicates that these may reflect real similarities among deaf readers.'

original_authors: Bem, D.
original_title: Feeling the future: Experimental evidence for anomalous retroactive influences on cognition and affect
