description: Performance on a memory recall test can be influenced by a post-test practice exercise, with participants recalling more words that they will later practice than control words (retroactive facilitation of recall)
justification: The authors explicitly state: "While Bem found a substantial effect, our results failed to provide any evidence for retroactive facilitation of recall." All three independent replication attempts produced non-significant results (combined p = .83, one-tailed).

original_authors: Cowan, F.; Pascoe, S.; Langhaug, L.; Mavhu, W.; Chidiya, S.; Jaffar, S.
original_title: The Regai Dzive Shiri Project: results of a randomised trial of an HIV prevention intervention for Zimbabwean youth
description: A multi-component community-based HIV prevention intervention program for young people reduces HIV and HSV-2 prevalence
justification: The pure replication confirmed the original null findings that the intervention did not reduce HIV or HSV-2 prevalence. However, dose-response analyses showed that high exposure to the intervention was associated with reduced risky sexual behaviors and "a trend towards reducing HIV or HSV-2 prevalence among males with a high-level exposure to the intervention" but not for females or the overall population.

original_authors: Hanslmayr, S.; Volberg, G.; Wimber, M.; Oehler, N.; Staudigl, T.; Hartmann, T.
original_title: Prefrontally driven downregulation of neural synchrony mediates goal-directed forgetting
description: 1Hz rTMS stimulation of left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) increases directed forgetting, causing participants to forget more to-be-forgotten items compared to vertex control stimulation
justification: The authors explicitly state "our results on their own should be interpreted as inconclusive." The direct replication found no significant increase in forgetting (p = 0.14), but when meta-analyzed with the original study, the combined effect was significant (g = 0.52, p = 0.02), leading the authors to conclude that "further replication attempts... is recommended to reliably demonstrate this causal role."

original_authors: Maier, M.; Buechner, V.; Kuhbandner, C.; Pflitsch, M.; Fernández-Capo, M.; Gámiz-Sanfeliu, M.
original_title: Feeling the future again: Retroactive avoidance of negative stimuli
description: Participants unconsciously avoid negative picture presentations that are randomly selected after their response, demonstrating retroactive avoidance of aversive stimuli
justification: The authors explicitly state: "our prediction was not substantiated, and the results reported by Maier et al. (Exp. 4, ES = 0.1) were not replicated in the present study" and conclude "no retroactive influences were detectable in this experiment" with a Bayes factor favoring the null hypothesis (BF₀₁ = 4.38).

original_authors: Glassenberg, A.; Feinberg, R.; Jones, B.; Little, A.; Debruine, L.
original_title: Sex-dimorphic face shape preference in heterosexual and homosexual men and women
description: Straight men show stronger preferences for feminized versions of women's faces than gay men do
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "This pattern of results replicates those reported by Glassenberg et al. [8]" and found a significant effect (p<0.001) showing straight men demonstrated stronger preferences for feminized women's faces than gay men.

original_authors: Glassenberg, A.; Feinberg, R.; Jones, B.; Little, A.; Debruine, L.
original_title: Sex-dimorphic face shape preference in heterosexual and homosexual men and women
description: Gay men show stronger preferences for masculinized versions of men's faces than straight men do
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "This pattern of results also replicates those reported by Glassenberg et al. [8]" and found a significant effect (p<0.001) showing gay men demonstrated stronger preferences for masculine men than straight men.

original_authors: Meyerholz, L.; Irzinger, J.; Witthöft, M.; Gerlach, A.; Pohl, A.
original_title: Contingent biofeedback outperforms other methods to enhance the accuracy of cardiac interoception: A comparison of short interventions
original_journal: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
description: Contingent biofeedback training improves cardiac interoceptive accuracy
justification: The authors explicitly concluded that "we did not observe the expected transfer-effect from the biofeedback training to the heartbeat discrimination task" and that "contingent cardiac biofeedback seems to not improve cardiac interoceptive accuracy." The observed effect (d = 0.15, p = .42) was over 20 million times more consistent with the null hypothesis than with the original large effect (d = 1.21), with a Bayes factor of 0.26 strongly supporting the null hypothesis.

original_authors: Sparks, A.; Barclay, P.
original_title: Eye images increase generosity, but not for long: The limited effect of a false cue
description: Images of eyes (eyespots) increase generosity in a dictator game by triggering feelings of observation and reputation management
justification: The authors explicitly state in their Discussion: "we failed to replicate the eyes effect... participants did not give more money in a dictator game when images of eyes were present compared to the control condition." Despite having 95% power to detect the effect, they found no difference between the eyes and control conditions.

original_authors: Simpson, B.; Willer, R.
original_title: Altruism and indirect reciprocity: The interaction of person and situation in prosocial behavior
description: People who are less prosocial (egoists) are more responsive to reputation-based cues than people who are more prosocial
justification: The authors report this as an exploratory analysis that "did not reach statistical significance" and note "this analysis was underpowered and we cannot draw definitive conclusions." However, they found results "suggestive" and "consistent with the prior study," with egoists giving less than prosocials in private but not public conditions.

original_authors: Neal, Z.; Neal, J.
original_title: Prevalence, age of decision, and interpersonal warmth judgements of childfree adults
description: Childfree adults comprise approximately 21% of the population, decide not to have children primarily during their teens and twenties, and parents exhibit strong in-group favoritism in interpersonal warmth judgements while childfree adults do not
justification: The authors state in their Discussion: "In this study, we directly replicated nearly all prior findings related to the prevalence, age of decision and interpersonal warmth judgements of childfree adults... Specifically, our study provides confirmatory evidence that childfree individuals are numerous, comprising over one in five Michigan adults, and tend to be early-deciders... Furthermore, we replicated prior evidence of ingroup favoritism in the interpersonal warmth judgements of parents."

original_authors: Taubert, J.
original_title: Chimpanzee faces are 'special' to humans
description: Chimpanzee faces engage special holistic processing mechanisms in humans, producing both disproportionate inversion effects and composite effects similar to human faces
justification: The authors state explicitly in the section header 'Experiment 4-An unsuccessful exact replication of Taubert (2009)' and in the discussion: 'Our direct replication of Experiment 2 from Taubert [33] has produced data that in no way match those reported in that study. There is no evidence from the replication that Chimpanzee faces have some kind of special status for Humans, as concluded by Taubert.'

original_authors: Job V; Dweck C; Walton G
original_title: Ego Depletion-Is It All in Your Head?: Implicit Theories About Willpower Affect Self-Regulation
description: The ego-depletion effect (performance decrease on a self-control task after performing another self-control task) occurs only for individuals who believe their willpower is limited
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "The current preregistered study failed to reproduce either the overall ego-depletion effect or its moderation by willpower mindset reported by Job et al." They conclude that the finding "is not a replicable finding that can provide a solid basis for rigorous theoretical development."

original_authors: Brandt, M.
original_title: Predicting Ideological Prejudice
description: Perceived ideology of target groups predicts the ideology-prejudice association more accurately than perceived status or choice in group membership
justification: The authors explicitly state in their Study 1 discussion: "This successful replication indicates Brandt's [1] models are robust across different types of absolute measures and across different samples" and "our results closely mirrored Brandt's [1] findings such that the status-only and choice-only models had weaker performances and were not significantly different from the null model."

original_authors: Smith, R.; Kirlic, N.; Stewart, J.
original_title: Greater decision uncertainty characterizes a transdiagnostic patient sample during approach avoidance conflict: a computational modelling approach
description: Individuals with depression/anxiety or substance use disorders show greater decision uncertainty (DU) and reduced emotion conflict (EC, reflecting reduced avoidance of negative stimuli) during approach-avoidance conflict tasks compared to healthy controls
justification: This is a partial replication. The authors state 'We successfully replicated and extended our previous findings' in the conclusion, but acknowledge that 'the previously observed difference in DU between participants with depression and/or anxiety disorders and healthy controls did not replicate.' The study successfully replicated greater DU in substance use disorders (p=0.026), reduced EC in substance use disorders (p<0.001, large effect), and reduced EC in females with depression/anxiety (p=0.007), but failed to replicate the DU effect in depression/anxiety (p=0.771).

original_authors: Rogenmoser, L.; Elmer, S.; Jäncke, L.
original_title: Absolute pitch: evidence for early cognitive facilitation during passive listening as revealed by reduced P3a amplitudes
description: Musicians with absolute pitch show smaller P3a amplitudes (an event-related potential component) compared to musicians without absolute pitch during passive listening to piano tones, suggesting early cognitive facilitation in absolute pitch processing
justification: The authors explicitly state: "However, and most critically, there were also no significant group differences in the P3a. Additional Bayes factor analyses revealed that the data are more likely under the null hypothesis...Thus, our results challenge the view of cognitive facilitation in AP during passive listening."

original_authors: Michalka, S.; Kong, L.; Rosen, M.; Shinn-Cunningham, B.; Somers, D.
original_title: Short-term memory for space and time flexibly recruit complementary sensorybiased frontal lobe attention networks
description: Visual and auditory working memory recruit distinct, anatomically interleaved sensory-biased regions in lateral frontal cortex (two bilateral visual-biased regions: sPCS and iPCS; two bilateral auditory-biased regions: tgPCS and cIFS)
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "Our findings: (1) provide strong replication of our prior report of two visual-biased regions interleaved with two auditory-biased regions bilaterally in LFC" and "Our results are a robust replication of earlier findings from our laboratory". All eight sensory-biased structures were identified in all 15 subjects, and seven subjects who participated in both studies showed high test-retest reliability (Dice coefficients 0.57-0.70).

original_authors: Pinel, P.; Fauchereau, F.; Moreno, A.; Barbot, A.; Lathrop, M.; Zelenika, D.; Bihan, L.; Poline, D.; Bourgeron, J.; Dehaene, T.; S.
original_title: Genetic variants of FOXP2 and KIAA0319/TTRAP/THEM2 locus are associated with altered brain activation in distinct language-related regions
description: The FOXP2 SNP rs6980093 is associated with left inferior frontal gyrus activation during sentence reading/listening, with activity increasing with the number of A alleles (AA>AG>GG)
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "Despite including a substantially larger sample, and a more powerful blocked design, we did not replicate the [33] associations. Formal Bayesian analyses yielded substantial-to-strong evidence supporting the null hypotheses for each SNP."

original_authors: Pinel, P.; Fauchereau, F.; Moreno, A.; Barbot, A.; Lathrop, M.; Zelenika, D.; Bihan, L.; Poline, D.; Bourgeron, J.; Dehaene, T.; S.
original_title: Genetic variants of FOXP2 and KIAA0319/TTRAP/THEM2 locus are associated with altered brain activation in distinct language-related regions
description: The FOXP2 SNP rs7784315 is associated with left precentral gyrus activation during sentence reading, with TC participants showing significantly higher activity than TT participants
justification: The Results section states: "We did not replicate this finding in either of the two visual subsamples." The Discussion confirms: "we did not replicate the [33] associations" with "substantial-to-strong evidence supporting the null hypotheses."

original_authors: Pinel, P.; Fauchereau, F.; Moreno, A.; Barbot, A.; Lathrop, M.; Zelenika, D.; Bihan, L.; Poline, D.; Bourgeron, J.; Dehaene, T.; S.
original_title: Genetic variants of FOXP2 and KIAA0319/TTRAP/THEM2 locus are associated with altered brain activation in distinct language-related regions
description: The KIAA0319/TTRAP/THEM2 SNP rs17243157 is associated with asymmetry of activation in the superior temporal sulcus during sentence reading/listening, with CC participants showing higher asymmetry than TC participants
justification: The Results section clearly states: "we did not replicate these associations in any of the subsamples." Bayesian analyses provided "substantial-to-strong evidence for non-replication" as stated in the Results and Discussion sections.

original_authors: Smith, R.; Webster, J.; Parrott, W.; Eyre, H.
original_title: The role of public exposure in moral and nonmoral shame and guilt
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
description: Public exposure of moral transgressions has a greater effect on shame than on guilt, distinguishing these two emotions based on exposure to others' scrutiny
justification: The authors explicitly conclude: "We therefore conclude this as a failed replication, not in support of the distinction made between shame and guilt in the target article (i.e., exposure)...we failed to find support that exposure had a greater effect on shame than guilt."

original_authors: Dreher, G.; Rüttermann, S.; Weberschock, S.
original_title: Conception and implementation of a novel E-learning module with EbM-learning contents in operative dentistry
description: An e-learning resource with dental case vignettes and evidence-based dentistry content receives positive ratings from dental students and is perceived as beneficial for their clinical coursework
justification: The authors state in the Results section: 'All obtained results in the replication study showed no statistical significant differences to the primary study.' The Discussion further confirms: 'The agreement of the results with those of the primary study points to the remarkable validity of the chosen method of evaluation.'

original_authors: Bleakley, H.
original_title: Malaria Eradication in the Americas: A Retrospective Analysis of Childhood Exposure
description: Large-scale malaria eradication campaigns in the 20th century led to increased adult income and human capital for those native to historically endemic areas
justification: The authors explicitly state in the abstract: 'I perform a pre-registered reanalysis and find these results to be largely robust. Malaria eradication efforts indeed appear to have been followed by anomalous income gains for natives of historically malarial areas of Brazil, Colombia, Mexico, and perhaps the United States.' The conclusion confirms: 'it broadly supports Bleakley's main result that the evidence indicates that eradication raised adult income.'

original_authors: Shimizu, Y.; Okada, K.; Karasawa, K.
original_title: 愛好家サブカテゴリーの顕現化によるギャンブラーへの潜在的態度の肯定化
description: Portraying non-stereotypical images of gamblers (recreational gamblers) improves implicit attitudes toward gamblers
justification: The authors explicitly state that 'The results showed no significant differences between the groups, and no meaningful changes in implicit attitudes after exposure to the recreational gambler vignette,' directly contradicting the original finding of a positive impact on implicit attitudes.

original_authors: Radin, D. I.
description: Physical proximity to sugar reduces grip strength in adult subjects
justification: The abstract explicitly states "Statistical analysis indicated no significant effect of held substance upon grip strength," directly contradicting Radin's original finding of a significant 4% reduction in grip strength when holding sugar.

original_authors: Onwuegbuzie, A.
original_title: Defense or offense? Which is the better predictor of success for professional football teams?
description: Defensive attainments (particularly turnover differential and rushing yards) are better predictors of NFL team success than offensive attainments
justification: The authors explicitly state that 'the present findings are consistent with the results of Onwuegbuzie who concluded that the attainments of the defense are more important than are the offensive attainments in predicting whether an NFL team will be successful.' The original two-variable model adequately predicted 1998-1999 season outcomes, and the new five-variable model showed defensive characteristics explaining over 75% of variance, with turnover differential remaining the strongest predictor (54.4% variance).

original_authors: Gabrys, J.; Peters, K.; Zong, W.
original_title: Reliability, discriminant and predictive validity of the Zung Selfrating Depression Scale
description: The Zung Self-Rating Depression Scale discriminates between depressed and non-depressed patients with good reliability and validity
justification: While the scale showed significant discrimination between groups (F=13.3, p=.0004), the authors noted "there is, however, considerably more overlap in group scores which makes prediction difficult for the individual case" and that "fewer depressed and nondepressed patients fell into the severe depression range" compared to Gabrys' original study, indicating a weaker replication.

original_authors: Jensen, M.; Kristiansen, I.; Sandbekk, M.; Kroger, J.
original_title: Ego identity status in cross-cultural context: a comparison of Norwegian and United States university students
description: Norwegian late adolescents score lower on extent of identity exploration and commitment compared to United States late adolescents in both ideological and interpersonal domains
justification: The authors explicitly state 'The present study replicates work by Jensen, et al. (1998)' and 'These results are consistent with findings of [Jensen et al.].' All differences were statistically significant (p < .001 for most), with moderate to large effect sizes (.56 to 2.07), confirming that Norwegian students scored consistently lower on all identity status scales.

original_authors: Bem, D.
original_title: Feeling the future: Experimental evidence for anomalous retroactive influences on cognition and affect
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
description: Response times to incongruent stimuli are longer than response times to congruent stimuli even though the prime appears after the participant's judgment (retroactive/precognitive priming effect)
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "Overall, the two studies did not replicate the original Bem findings for time-reverse priming on RT. Both failed to reach significance in the preplanned confirmatory hypotheses." Neither Experiment 1 nor Experiment 2 showed significant effects in their pre-registered confirmatory analyses.

original_authors: Ross, C.; Engle, C.; Baker, B.
original_title: Reductions in symptomatology at a residential treatment center for substance use disorder
description: Multimodal, trauma-informed residential treatment for substance use disorders produces marked reductions in symptoms of depression, anxiety, dissociation, and PTSD from admission to discharge
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'The data in the present sample (N=200) replicated the findings in the prior sample (N=100).' The Results section confirms that scores on all four symptom measures (BDI, BAI, DES, PCL-C) at both admission and discharge did not differ between the original and replication samples at p = .05, demonstrating successful replication of the symptom reduction pattern.

original_authors: Dreßing, H.; Kuehner, C.; Gass, P.
original_title: Lifetime prevalence and impact of stalking in a European population: epidemiological data from a middlesized German city
description: Stalking has a lifetime prevalence of approximately 11-12% in German adults aged 18-65, with victims showing elevated rates of mental disorders compared to non-victims
justification: The authors state: 'The lifetime prevalence of stalking in the 2018 sample was 10.8%, close to the figure of 11.6% in 2003' and 'Both in 2003 and in 2018, the mental disorders of stalking victims were more severe than those in persons who had not been exposed to stalking... the data confirm the findings' from the original study.

original_authors: Remmers, C.; Topolinski, S.; Dietrich, D.; Michalak, J.
original_title: Impaired intuition in patients with major depressive disorder
description: Patients with major depression show deficits in intuitively detecting semantic coherence compared to healthy controls
justification: The authors explicitly state in their discussion: 'the current study did not replicate findings from previous research regarding intuitive semantic coherence detection deficits in depression.' The main hypothesis (H1) that depressed patients would be less able to discriminate semantic coherence was not supported: t(68) = -0.12, p = .90.

original_authors: Zimmerman, B.; Kitsantas, A.
original_title: Comparing Students' Self-Discipline and Self-Regulation Measures and Their Prediction of Academic Achievement
description: Self-regulation (but not self-discipline) uniquely predicts academic achievement (GPA) when controlling for both constructs
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: "we found support for that claim: self-regulation of effort was moderately predictive of semester GPA at the university. Self-discipline was not associated with GPA over and above self-regulation effort." The replication successfully confirmed the original finding despite a smaller effect size.

original_authors: Bortoletto, M.; Bonzano, L.; Zazio, A.; Ferrari, C.; Pedullà, L.; Gasparotti, R.
original_title: Asymmetric transcallosal conduction delay leads to finer bimanual coordination
description: M1-P15 amplitude positively predicts ipsilateral silent period (iSP) magnitude, reflecting transcallosal inhibition between motor cortices
justification: The authors explicitly state: 'we show a replication of the relationship between M1-P15 and iSP' and in the conclusion write 'as revealed by the successful replication of its positive relationship with the iSP' (p = 0.001).

original_authors: Bortoletto, M.; Bonzano, L.; Zazio, A.; Ferrari, C.; Pedullà, L.; Gasparotti, R.
original_title: Asymmetric transcallosal conduction delay leads to finer bimanual coordination
description: M1-P15 latency (transcallosal conduction delay) predicts bimanual coordination performance in sequential thumb-to-finger opposition movements
justification: The authors state: 'Contrary to our expectations, we did not observe any significant relationship between the M1-P15 latency and behavioral performance' (all p > 0.07). They conclude the 'discrepancies between this study and our previous one highlight the need for future investigations'.

original_authors: Filbrich, L.; Van Den Broeke, E.; Legrain, V.; Mouraux, A.
original_title: The focus of spatial attention during the induction of central sensitization can modulate the subsequent development of secondary hyperalgesia
description: Focusing spatial attention on one forearm during bilateral high-frequency electrical stimulation increases mechanical pinprick sensitivity (secondary hyperalgesia) on the attended arm compared to the unattended arm
justification: The authors explicitly state: "We therefore did not replicate the observations made by [Filbrich et al. 2020]. Both confirmatory and sensitivity analyses showed that there was no significant difference between the two arms compared in terms of percentage of change in mechanical pinprick sensitivity."

original_authors: Eikeseth, F. F.; Denninghaus, S.; Cropley, M.; Witthöft, M.; Pawelzik, M.; Sütterlin, S.
original_title: The cortisol awakening response at admission to hospital predicts depression severity after discharge in major depressive disorder (MDD) patients
description: A blunted cortisol awakening response (CAR) at admission to hospital predicts higher depression severity six weeks and six months after discharge in major depressive disorder patients
justification: The authors state "Our former reported results (Eikeseth et al., 2019) have been partly replicated" with comparable effect sizes (r = -0.223 vs r = -0.213 original), but the main analysis did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.054), leading them to conclude it "largely replicated previous (significant) findings" but with "statistically non-significant" results.

original_authors: Schmitt, V.; Fischer, J.
original_title: Representational format determines numerical competence in monkeys
description: Monkeys (olive baboons and long-tailed macaques) perform better at quantity discrimination when choosing between inedible items or when choosing between edible items but receiving different edible items as rewards, compared to choosing and receiving the same edible items
justification: The authors state: "Interestingly, the horses were indifferent to the type of choice stimuli that were presented, i.e., they were not more or less successful when they chose between slices of apple than when they chose between wooden blocks." The GLMM revealed no significant effect of stimulus type (P = 0.606), and overall the horses showed at-chance performance with no evidence of quantity discrimination abilities.

original_authors: Heinemann, A.; Kunde, W.; Kiesel, A.
original_title: Context-specific primecongruency effects: On the role of conscious stimulus representations for cognitive control
description: Context-specific proportion congruency effects occur only with conscious conflict stimuli, not with unconscious conflict stimuli, indicating that cognitive control requires consciousness
justification: The authors state 'we failed to replicate the results described by [18]' and found a CSPC effect in both conscious and unconscious groups (contrary to the original). However, they also note 'caution is warranted' because the effect 'was only observable on test trials, and not on inducing trials,' was absent in RTs in Experiment 1, and 'was not observed consistently' in Experiment 2 when considering only trials within the response deadline.

original_authors: Vul, E.; Pashler, H.
original_title: Measuring the crowd within: probabilistic representations within individuals
description: The average of two estimates from one person tends to be more accurate than a single estimate from that person (the 'crowd within' effect)
justification: The authors explicitly state in their Discussion: "Our replication attempt of the crowd within effect supports the original finding by Vul and Pashler (2008) that averaging two guesses within one person provides a more accurate answer than either guess alone... These results were evaluated as successful replications against two different replication evaluation standards."

original_authors: Tversky, A.
original_title: Features of similarity
description: The diagnosticity principle determines which features are used to cluster multiple objects into subgroups, with perceived similarity between items within clusters increasing while similarity between items in different clusters decreases
justification: The authors state: "without eliminating possible substitution effects we replicate the original findings by [9] and [10]. However, eliminating substitution effects strongly reduces the observed differences between conditions." They conclude: "There are two explanations that seem likely... One possibility is that there really are no diagnosticity effects... The other explanation could be that diagnosticity effects do exist but only in situations where the features of the targets are visual and readily available."

original_authors: Tversky, A.; Gati, I.
original_title: Studies of similarity
description: The diagnosticity principle applies to similarity judgments of countries where categorization influences perceived similarity based on semantic knowledge rather than visual features
justification: The authors found that "The results of Study 2a, and 2b are also very similar to those originally observed by [10], but again revealed smaller effects." However, after eliminating substitution effects, they report: "eliminating substitution effects strongly reduces the observed differences between conditions with averages of... -1.21% (2a), and 1.24% (2b)" clustering around zero, leading to inconclusive evidence for the diagnosticity effect.

original_authors: Kurzban, R.; Tooby, J.; Cosmides, L.
original_title: Can race be erased? Coalitional computation and social categorization
description: When coalitional cues are orthogonal to racial cues, the tendency to categorize people on the basis of their race is strongly reduced
justification: While both hypotheses were statistically confirmed (p = 0.023 for race reduction; p < 0.001 for coalition increase), the authors emphasize that "the effect size of the reduction in race encoding was considerably smaller than the effect sizes reported by [8]" and "the evidence for a reduction in race encoding was rather weak" with only "anecdotal" Bayesian support (BF = 1.82).

original_authors: Buccino, G.; Riggio, L.; Melli, G.; Binkofski, F.; Gallese, V.; Rizzolatti, G.
original_title: Listening to action-related sentences modulates the activity of the motor system: a combined TMS and behavioural study
description: Listening to hand-related sentences decreases motor evoked potentials (MEPs) recorded from hand muscles compared to foot-related sentences, reflecting an interference effect in the motor system during language processing
justification: The authors found the opposite effect: "our data showed an early modulation of MEPs... However, the direction of the effect is reversed with respect to [5], where an interference effect was shown. Namely, hand MEPs increased in response to hand-related action sentences" - they found facilitation instead of interference.

original_authors: Buccino, G.; Riggio, L.; Melli, G.; Binkofski, F.; Gallese, V.; Rizzolatti, G.
original_title: Listening to action-related sentences modulates the activity of the motor system: a combined TMS and behavioural study
description: Reaction times are slower when the body effector used to give motor responses matches the effector involved in the action expressed by the presented verb, reflecting an interference effect
justification: The authors explicitly state: "Despite more than doubling the number of participants, we were unable to replicate the most significant findings in the behavioral experiment. In particular, we were not able to get significant results in the crucial 'sentence' × 'effector' interaction."

original_authors: Topolinski, S.; Sparenberg, P.
original_title: Turning the hands of time: clockwise movements increase preference for novelty
description: Clockwise movements induce psychological states of temporal progression and orientation toward the future and novelty, specifically increasing openness to experience
justification: The authors explicitly state: "We were unable to replicate the finding reported by Topolinski and Sparenberg (2012, Experiment 2). Based on data from 102 participants, our preregistered Bayes factor hypothesis test revealed that the data were 10.76 times more likely under the null hypothesis than under the alternative hypothesis."

original_authors: McElree, B.; Foraker, S.; Dyer, L.
original_title: Memory structures that subserve sentence comprehension
description: During sentence comprehension, readers use a content-addressable direct-access retrieval mechanism to retrieve grammatical dependencies, characterized by decreased accuracy but constant retrieval speed as distance increases between dependent elements
justification: The authors explicitly state: "The results of this experiment replicate McElree and colleagues' demonstration of direct-access retrieval" and "Our results replicate previous findings that suggest that a direct-access retrieval mechanism supports online parsing operations." Experiment 1 successfully reproduced the signature pattern of direct-access retrieval using auditory stimuli.

original_authors: Kraus, M.; Tan, J.
original_title: Americans overestimate social class mobility
description: Americans substantially overestimate social class mobility in society, provide greater overestimates when thinking of similar others, and those with high perceived social class provide larger overestimates
justification: The authors explicitly state: "The results from this preregistered exact replication of Study 3 from [9] provide evidence consistent with each of these three predictions" and found that "Participants provided large overestimates of social class mobility that became even larger when considered for individuals similar to the self" with effect sizes similar to or larger than the original.

original_authors: Ameel, E.; Storms, G.; Malt, B.; Sloman, S.
original_title: How bilinguals solve the naming problem
description: Bilinguals converge their naming patterns across both languages, forming a partially merged naming pattern rather than maintaining two separate monolingual-like naming patterns
justification: The authors explicitly state: "This conceptual replication study offers confirmatory evidence for a converged naming pattern in adult bilinguals as demonstrated by [3][4]" and "we succeeded in replicating these experiments... We successfully replicated the group-level analysis with correlation contrasts."

original_authors: Ameel, E.; Malt, B.; Storms, G.; Van Assche, F.
original_title: Semantic convergence in the bilingual lexicon
description: Bilingual category centers in multidimensional semantic space are closer to each other than monolingual category centers, indicating convergence at both category boundaries and centers
justification: The authors state: "More evidence for converged naming patterns was found in a representation in a multidimensional space and the finding of shorter distances between bilingual category centers than monolingual category centers... These findings show that convergence takes place at both category boundaries and category centers" confirming the findings of Ameel et al. (2009).

original_authors: Muffato, V.; Hilton, C.; Meneghetti, C.; De Beni, R.; Wiener, J.
original_title: Evidence for age-related deficits in object-location binding during place recognition
description: Older adults show impaired place recognition ability, particularly when object-location binding is required (swap condition), but preserved spatial perspective-taking ability compared to younger adults
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion section: 'We replicated behavioural findings reported by [41]' and 'The behavioural results of this study are a direct replication of those found by [41].' They confirmed that older adults performed worse than younger adults, particularly in the swap condition requiring object-location binding.

original_authors: Lee, H.; Seong, E.; Choi, W.; Lowder, M.
original_title: Development and assessment of the korean author recognition test
description: Print exposure measured by the Korean Author Recognition Test (KART) correlates with language skills and modulates the word frequency effect in lexical decision tasks, such that individuals with higher KART scores show smaller frequency effects
justification: The authors explicitly state: "the results reported here serve as a successful replication of all the key results reported in Lee et al." They replicated all three main findings: correlations between KART and language measures, and the critical interaction showing KART scores modulate word frequency effects.

original_authors: Popp, E.; Serra, M.
original_title: Animacy enhances free recall but impairs cued recall
original_journal: J. Exp. Psychol. Learn. Mem. Cogn
description: Free recall performance is better for animal names than for inanimate object names (animacy effect)
justification: The authors state in their discussion: "our primary analyses yielded results that closely paralleled theirs. Free recall was better for animal names than object names" and in their conclusion that "The results of our experiments...suggest that the reverse animacy effect in cued recall is a robust, replicable effect."

original_authors: Popp, E.; Serra, M.
original_title: Animacy enhances free recall but impairs cued recall
original_journal: J. Exp. Psychol. Learn. Mem. Cogn
description: Cued recall performance is better for inanimate object-object pairs than for animal-animal pairs (reverse animacy effect)
justification: The authors explicitly state: "Overall, we replicated the basic pattern observed by Popp and Serra (2016): better free recall for animals than objects, and better cued recall for objects than animals" and conclude that the effect is "robust" and "replicable."

original_authors: Gould, S.; Norton, W.
original_title: The Mismeasure of Man: Revised and Expanded
original_journal: The Mismeasure of Man: Revised and Expanded
description: The Army Beta intelligence test had inappropriate content, unsuitable administration conditions, impossibly short time limits, and could not have measured intelligence in illiterate or non-English speaking World War I draftees
justification: The authors explicitly state in their discussion: 'Gould's criticism of time limits and his argument that the Army Beta did not measure intelligence are without basis' and conclude 'We believe that Stephen Jay Gould was largely incorrect in his assessments of the Army Beta.' Their replication demonstrated that the Army Beta did measure intelligence and had appropriate content, instructions, and time limits.

original_authors: Tsay, C.
original_title: The vision heuristic: Judging music ensembles by sight alone
description: Musical novices can successfully judge the winner of music competitions from 6-second silent video clips at above-chance rates
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: "In this direct, well-powered replication, we observed a null effect... we argue that these findings should be given precedence over the original findings" and "the claim being tested was not found to replicate successfully, suggesting that the original result may have been a false positive finding."

original_authors: Taguchi, T.; Magid, M.; Papi, M.
original_title: The L2 motivational system amongst Japanese, Chinese, and Iranian learners of English: A comparative study
original_journal: Motivation, language identity and the L2 self
description: The L2 motivational self system (comprising ideal L2 self, ought-to L2 self, and L2 learning experience) provides a culture-independent explanation of second language learning motivation and its relationship with learners' preference for and effort to learn the second language
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion that 'Our results support the findings of Taguchi et al.' and 'our study provides evidence supporting the explanatory power of the tripartite model of the L2 motivational self originally tested by Taguchi et al.' The structural equation modeling confirmed the validity of the model with acceptable goodness-of-fit indices.

original_authors: Manwell, L.; Roberts, M.; Besner, D.
original_title: Single letter coloring and spatial cuing eliminates a semantic contribution to the Stroop effect
description: Coloring and cuing a single letter (versus all letters) in a word eliminates the semantically based Stroop effect
justification: The authors explicitly state: "contrary to Manwell et al.'s results but in line with those obtained by Augustinova and Ferrand, these manipulations consistently failed to eliminate or even reduce the semantically based Stroop effect." Both experiments found significant semantic Stroop effects with single-letter coloring, directly contradicting the original study's claim of elimination.

original_authors: Weissman, D. H.; Jiang, J.; Egner, T.
original_title: Determinants of congruency sequence effects without learning and memory confounds
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance
description: The congruency sequence effect (CSE) appears only in tasks where the distractor can be translated into a response faster than the target, specifically in prime-probe and Simon tasks but not in flanker and Stroop tasks
justification: The replication found the CSE in all four tasks (prime-probe, flanker, Stroop, and Simon) in RT, extending beyond the original which only found it in prime-probe and Simon tasks. The authors state 'our results extend but do not fundamentally contradict the original findings' and conclude 'it seems premature to conclude that the difference in the speed of distractor-vs target-related response activation is a determinant of the size of cross-trial modulations of control,' contradicting the original's theoretical interpretation.

original_authors: Brady, T.; Alvarez, G.
original_title: Hierarchical encoding in visual working memory: Ensemble statistics bias memory for individual items
description: Memory for the size of individual colored circles is biased toward the mean size of same-colored circles in the group
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: "The obtained results provide strong evidence in favor of the alternative hypothesis over the null hypothesis. Thus, our results replicate the main finding of Brady and Alvarez (2011), although with a smaller effect size." They found a significant bias (p < .001, d = 0.23) and strong Bayesian evidence (BF₁₀ = 634,953).

original_authors: Yi, H.; Phelps, J.; Smiljanic, R.; Chandrasekaran, B.
original_title: Reduced efficiency of audiovisual integration for nonnative speech
original_journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
description: Audiovisual benefit (improvement in speech intelligibility when seeing the talker in addition to hearing their voice) is smaller for nonnative-accented speech compared to native-accented speech
justification: The authors state in their interim discussion: "We replicated the finding that audiovisual benefit is reduced for nonnative-accented speech." This finding was confirmed across both experiments.

original_authors: Yi, H.; Phelps, J.; Smiljanic, R.; Chandrasekaran, B.
original_title: Reduced efficiency of audiovisual integration for nonnative speech
original_journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
description: Individual differences in implicit racial biases (as measured by Implicit Association Tests) predict the magnitude of reduced audiovisual benefit for nonnative versus native speech
justification: The authors explicitly state: "we did not replicate the finding that implicit racial biases (as measured by an IAT) are related to the magnitude of this effect... our results did not support the conclusion that implicit racial biases... were related to these differences in audiovisual benefit."

original_authors: Casasanto, D.; Boroditsky, L.
original_title: Time in the mind: Using space to think about time
description: Spatial information influences temporal estimates asymmetrically (space affects time judgments more than time affects space judgments), supporting metaphor theory over ATOM
justification: The authors explicitly state in their Discussion: "Our pre-registered analyses provide robust and conclusive evidence against metaphor theory, in favor of ATOM" and "there is not good evidence that there is substantial asymmetry as was reported in [Casasanto & Boroditsky 2008]." They found a symmetrical relationship (both effects ~2.8% variance) rather than the original's asymmetric pattern (94% vs 5%).

original_authors: Brady, T.; Shafer-Skelton, A.; Alvarez, G.
original_title: Global ensemble texture representations are critical to rapid scene perception
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance
description: Texturized scene images that preserve global ensemble texture statistics can prime scene perception, but texturized object images cannot prime object perception, suggesting separate processing pathways for scenes versus objects
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: 'we were unable to replicate the critical conditions from Brady et al. (2017). Thus, we do not find sufficient evidence for a privileged role of global ensemble statistics for scene over object perception.' Unlike the original study, they found priming effects for both texturized objects AND texturized scenes, contradicting the key finding that only scenes show this effect.

original_authors: Wolford, G.; Newman, S.; Miller, M.; Wig, G.
original_title: Searching for patterns in random sequences
description: A concurrent verbal working memory task (n-back) reduces probability matching and increases probability maximizing in repeated binary choice, improving decision-making by taxing cognitive resources needed for pattern search
justification: The authors explicitly state: "We were unable to replicate the beneficial effect of cognitive load on maximization in repeated binary choice reported by Wolford et al. (2004)" and "our preregistered replication study revealed no statistically significant effects of cognitive load on strategy selection" with Bayesian analysis providing evidence in favor of the null hypothesis (BF = 4.31).

original_authors: Jha, A.; Kiyonaga, A.
original_title: Working-memory-triggered dynamic adjustments in cognitive control
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
description: High mnemonic load in a working memory task triggers dynamic adjustments in cognitive control, resulting in enhanced performance on subsequent trials
justification: The authors explicitly state: 'these results demonstrated a replication of a prior study regarding the upregulation of cognitive control as a function of mnemonic demands' and 'The findings that high versus low mnemonic load resulted in subsequent-trial performance benefits over two experiments, herein, replicate the prior findings by Jha and Kiyonaga (2010).'

original_authors: Mehta, R.; Zhu, R.
original_title: Blue or red? Exploring the effect of color on cognitive task performances
description: Red background color decreases solution times for avoidance-motivation anagrams, and blue background color decreases solution times for approach-motivation anagrams
justification: The authors explicitly state in their Discussion: 'The results failed to confirm the interaction effect and the specific contrasts reported by Mehta and Zhu (2009)... The results of the direct replication here have called into question the color-priming effect on anagram solution times.' The predicted interaction was not significant (p = .12).

original_authors: Rayner, K.; Balota, D.; Pollatsek, A.
original_title: Against parafoveal semantic preprocessing during eye fixations in reading
description: Readers obtain orthographic preview benefit but not semantic preview benefit when reading words in parafoveal vision during English reading
justification: The authors explicitly state in their Discussion: 'In a close replication of [28], we found no evidence of semantic preview benefit. Thus, with respect to the issue implicitly raised by [17], the results reported by Rayner et al. are replicable.' The study successfully replicated the original finding of orthographic but not semantic preview benefit.

original_authors: Newell, B.; Rakow, T.; Yechiam, E.; Sambur, M.
original_title: Rare disaster information can increase risk-taking
description: Providing rare disaster information increases people's tolerance for risk-taking
justification: The authors explicitly state: "the effect did not replicate in this registered replication" and "our various examinations of the disaster information effect over the past couple of years suggest that it is fickle... Taken together, these results imply that any effect of feedback is small."

original_authors: Bruderer, A.; Danielson, D.; Kandhadai, P.; Werker, J.
original_title: Sensorimotor influences on speech perception in infancy
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
description: Restricting tongue-tip movement with a teething toy interferes with 6-month-old infants' discrimination of the non-native dental /da/ vs. retroflex /Da/ phonetic contrast
justification: Experiment 1 successfully replicated discrimination without the teether (p=0.024), and Experiment 2 successfully replicated the disruption effect when tongue-tip movement was restricted (p=0.98, BF01=4.66). The authors explicitly state: "Results from Experiment 1 replicate the previous findings" and "infants' lack of discrimination, shown here with synthesized stimuli, replicates the findings reported in Experiment 2 of Bruderer et al. (2015)."

original_authors: Brielmann, A.; Pelli, D.
original_title: Tracking two pleasures (pilot study)
description: People can faithfully track and report the pleasure from each of two simultaneously presented images and can accurately report the average pleasure of both images
justification: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'All the main results of the original study with 13 observers (Supplementary Pilot Study) were replicated with 25 observers' and in the Conclusion: 'All the main results of the original study with 13 observers were replicated with 25 observers.' The abstract confirms: 'Our replication confirms the original study.'

original_authors: Béna, J.; Rihet, M.; Carreras, O.; Terrier, P.
original_title: Repetition could increase the perceived truth of conspiracy theories
description: Repetition increases the perceived truth of conspiracy statements (the illusory truth effect), with the effect being smaller for conspiracy statements than trivia statements
justification: The authors explicitly state their hypothesis was confirmed: "Consistent with our hypothesis, there were no significant differences in the magnitude of the illusory truth effect between conspiracy and trivia statements when matching statements based on baseline plausibility in our preregistered analyses." This successfully replicates the core finding while demonstrating that the original difference was due to baseline plausibility rather than statement type.

original_authors: Sirieix, L.; Remaud, H.; Lockshin, L.; Thach, L.; Lease, T.
original_title: Determinants of restaurant owner/managers selection of wines to be offered on the wine list
original_journal: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
description: Restaurateurs prioritize matching wine with food and taste quality as the most important factors when selecting wines for restaurant wine lists
justification: The study successfully replicated the top two most important factors (matching wine with food and taste), but found differences in the ranking of other factors. The authors conclude that there are 'similarities and differences' and note that 'the factors that were found to explain decisions in a particular geographical area cannot merely be accepted as factors for decision-making in other areas,' indicating partial replication.

original_authors: Uçkun, B.
original_title: How does context contribute to EFL learners' assessment of vocabulary gain
description: Different levels of context in vocabulary assessment (matching vs. sentence-level gap filling vs. rational-deletion cloze) produce significantly different test scores, with no significant difference between matching and sentence-level questions
justification: The authors explicitly state that their results differed from Uçkun's findings: 'Results from the ANOVA differ from the findings from Uçkun's study (2008). In her study, there was no significant difference between scores on the matching and sentence-level questions... The results of the present study indicate that the nonsignificant difference is between sentence and paragraph.' The Conclusion confirms: 'Results showed that there was a significant difference between no-context and contextualized test questions... which was contrary to the original study.'

original_authors: Sénémeaud, C.; Sanrey, C.; Callé, N.; Plainfossé, C.; Belhaire, A.; Georget, P.
original_title: The watchingeyes phenomenon and blood donation: Does exposure to pictures of eyes increase blood donation by young adults?
description: Exposure to pictures of eyes on a poster increases blood donation behavior among young adults
justification: The authors explicitly state: "Overall, we failed to replicate the watching-eyes effect despite using a considerably larger sample than previous studies. The effect of the eye-like image was not significant regardless of whether there was a pro-blood donation norm."

original_authors: Fujikawa, M.; Yokota, K.; Tokuoka, M.; Nakanishi, D.
original_title: Can conformity bias be observed in questions whose answers are objectively fixed?
description: Conformist bias (tendency to conform to majority responses exceeding the actual proportion) can be observed when individuals answer questions with objectively fixed correct answers
justification: The replication produced mixed results that differ from the original study. The authors state: "the finding that conformist bias was only observed for objective questions differs from the findings of Fujikawa et al. (2024)" - the original found conformist bias for both objective and attitude questions, while this replication found it only for objective questions.

original_authors: Sainte-Laudy, J.; Belon, P.
original_title: Improvement of flow cytometric analysis of basophil activation inhibition by high histamine dilutions. A novel basophil specific marker: CD 203c
description: Highly diluted histamine (15cH, 16cH) inhibits human basophil activation as measured by CD203c membrane up-regulation
justification: The authors explicitly state: 'No difference in basophil activation was observed between the highly diluted histamine samples and the highly diluted water controls' and 'our results do not confirm the large inhibitory effects observed for histamine 15cH and 16cH.'

original_authors: Scherr, C.; Simon, M.; Spranger, J.; Baumgartner, S.
original_title: Effects of potentised substances on growth rate of the water plant Lemna gibba L
description: Homeopathic potencies of gibberellic acid (15x-24x) reduce growth rate of Lemna gibba L. (duckweed)
justification: Mixed results across three experimental series: two series found no significant effects (p=0.263, p=0.062), while the third series found a significant effect (p=0.009) but in the opposite direction (growth increased rather than decreased as in the original study).

original_authors: Baron, J.; Hershey, J.
original_title: Outcome bias in decision evaluation
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
description: Decisions that resulted in successful outcomes are rated as better quality than decisions that resulted in failed outcomes, even when the decisions themselves are identical
justification: The authors explicitly state in their Discussion section: "We concluded a successful replication with signal and direction consistent with that of the target article's findings" and "Overall, the present study can be considered a successful replication attempt." They successfully replicated outcome bias with larger effect sizes (patient: original d = 0.21, replication d = 0.77; physician: original d = 0.53, replication d = 1.1).

original_authors: Bastian, B.; Loughnan, S.; Haslam, N.; Radke, H.
original_title: Don't mind meat? The denial of mind to animals used for human consumption
description: Animals perceived as more edible are attributed less sophisticated minds, feeling bad about eating animals is positively related to mind attribution, and moral concern for animals is positively related to mind attribution
justification: The authors state: 'Overall, the findings convincingly replicated Study 1 from Bastian et al. (2012)' and 'For Study 1, the effect sizes were remarkably similar to the original.' All three hypotheses were supported with strong correlations in the expected directions.

original_authors: Bastian, B.; Loughnan, S.; Haslam, N.; Radke, H.
original_title: Don't mind meat? The denial of mind to animals used for human consumption
description: Learning that an animal will be used for food leads people to attribute less sophisticated minds to that animal compared to when it will not be used for food
justification: The authors state: 'Thus, we concluded a successful replication of Study 2 from Bastian et al. (2012)' and in the general discussion: 'Overall, we conclude a successful replication.' The effect was significant in the same direction, though slightly weaker (d = 0.30 vs. original d = 0.40).

original_authors: Monin, B.; Miller, D.
original_title: Moral credentials and the expression of prejudice
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
description: Having an opportunity to hire a job candidate from disadvantaged groups (establishing moral credentials) licenses people to subsequently express preferences that are more likely to be perceived as prejudiced.
justification: The authors explicitly state: 'We could not replicate the original findings' and 'We failed to replicate the findings of Study 2 in [50] about the moral credential effect.' The effect was close to zero in the ethnicity scenario (d = 0.02 to 0.08) and reversed in the gender scenario (d = -0.50 to -0.38), showing a moral consistency effect rather than a moral licensing effect.

original_authors: Pronin, E.; Kugler, M.
original_title: People believe they have more free will than others
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
description: People believe their own decisions and life events are less predictable than those of others, suggesting higher free will attributions
justification: The authors state they found a 'mostly successful replication' but with 'considerably smaller' effect sizes than the original. Study 1a showed support (d=-0.84), Study 1b had just-barely-detectable effects (d=-0.30, p=.046), Study 2 between-subjects replicated the effect (d=-0.33), but Study 2 within-subjects found no support (d=0.00, p=.490). The authors note 'weaker to no support for the effect when we ran a novel within-subject design.'

original_authors: Letts
original_title: Highly reproducible LENR experiments using dual laser stimulation
description: Dual-laser stimulation at specific THz difference frequencies (around 8, 15, and 20 THz) triggers excess heat production (100-300 mW) in loaded palladium deuteride cathodes
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusions: 'Despite having replicated Letts' original experimental design and protocol to the best of our ability, and conducting 231 attempts across 9 cathode runs, we did not observe evidence of laser-triggered excess heat events on the order of 100 mW reported by Letts. The average excess heat rate observed from all runs was 6.1 ± 21.6 mW with ⇠10 W of input electrical power.'

original_authors: Stoffel M; Caspers B; Forcada J; Giannakara A; Baier M; Eberhart-Phillips L; Müller C; Hoffman J
original_title: Chemical fingerprints encode mother-offspring similarity, colony membership, relatedness, and genetic quality in fur seals
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
description: Antarctic fur seals from different breeding colonies exhibit chemically distinct signatures, and mothers show chemical similarity to their pups
justification: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: "Both hypotheses were supported by our data" and in the discussion note that "the effect sizes of patterns of colony membership and mother-offspring similarity...were of similar magnitude in a new sample of mother-offspring pairs separated by 5 years." All p-values remained highly significant (p < 0.0001) and effect sizes differed by only a few percent.

original_authors: Perea M; Acha J; Fraga I
original_title: Lexical competition is enhanced in the left hemisphere: evidence from different types of orthographic neighbors
description: Words with larger orthographic neighborhoods (more neighbors) show a facilitatory effect in the left visual field but an inhibitory or weaker effect in the right visual field during lexical decision tasks
justification: The authors explicitly state they met all three pre-registered criteria for successful replication: 'Analysis of error rates and reaction times met our three criteria for successful replication... a facilitative N effect in the left visual field and an inhibitory effect in the right visual field in reaction times for word targets. This pattern of results replicates several prior studies and confirms predictions from the SERIOL model.'
